items.body: If you’re a regular reader here, you’d know by now what I search for the most in new music is something that I’ve never heard before. BJ Cole and Secondson’s new pedal steel guitar and Cristal Baschet duo record, There is Wonder Here, is exactly that. Available 9/18 from Centripetal Force on CD, vinyl and digital (and on cassette through Geology Records), this album is a dreamy and otherworldly set of soundscapes and experimental compositions that break through the boundaries of ambient Americana music into something completely new and original. So what makes this album so particularly unique? Well, for starters, BJ Cole is one of the most groundbreaking and influential pedal steel players ever, known for mastering and expanding the horizons of his instrument through collaborations with the likes of The Orb, Björk, John Cale and Brian Eno (plus famously appearing on Elton John’s “Tiny Dancer,”). Yet it’s his distinctive approach to the instrument combined with the utterly incomparable sound of the Cristal Baschet that makes this LP stand apart from anything else you might find in the record shop today. Seen here in this image that I absolutely borrowed from Wikipeida A Cristal Baschet is sort of like a glass harmonica, with gentle, vocal-like tones and great oscillating Cathedral pipe organ-like resonances that are produced by rubbing chromatically tuned glass rods with wet fingertips. Secondson has described the rare instrument as “an acoustic synthesizer,” and its ghostly drones and shimmering tones blend sympathetically with the similarly sweeping, ethereal sounds of the pedal steel. When played together, the effect is expansive, transfixing and downright moving. Photo by Rhodri Brooks Photo by Rhodri Brooks While you might expect music from this particular combination of instruments to be purely minimal and amorphous, you’d be surprised to find that these tracks are actual songs with melodies and tight structures. Check out “A Place You Could Never Leave,” the album’s first single, for example: With the way this track sways, dances and ebbs and flows, it’s almost lyrical. This particular song, and several others on this record, even has the vibe of a grand orchestral piecee that echoes the work of some of the more progressive modernist American classical composers of the 20th century. Fans of North Americans, Keith Jarrett’s Hymns/Spheres and Mark Korven’s soundtrack to Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse will surely appreciate the beauty and genius of this duo record. Click here to preorder your copy today. -KH
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由踏板钢棒吉他手BJ Cole与Cristal Baschet演奏者Secondson合作，以两种罕见乐器构建出梦幻而超验的声音景观。Cristal Baschet被形容为“原声合成器”，其玻璃音棒产生的教堂管风琴式共振与踏板钢棒的滑音交融，形成既空旷又富有歌唱性的质感。尽管乐器组合看似极简，作品却具备完整的旋律与紧凑结构，例如单曲《A Place You Could Never Leave》在起伏中呈现近乎管弦乐的宏大气质，并呼应20世纪美国现代主义作曲家的某些倾向。专辑由Centripetal Force发行，适合喜爱North Americans、Keith Jarrett《Hymns/Spheres》及Mark Korven配乐的听众。

items.body: Gelareh Pour and Brian O’Dwyer build each show live, on the spot, from a kamancheh, a voice, and a drum kit. Nine years into the project, that’s made them genuinely hard to predict, even for themselves. Pour grew up in Iran, where the path to a singing career ran through very narrow lanes for a woman; she carried that instrument and that history with her to Australia, where she met O’Dwyer, a drummer with a strong ear for improvisation and a real curiosity about where Persian tradition could go next. Together they’ve picked up an Art Music Award for Excellence in Experimental Practice in 2024, and travelled to the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity in Canada to record their third album in a single live pass, each take committed to tape as it happened. Its title, May The Devil’s Ear Be Deaf, comes from an old Persian phrase spoken after voicing something beautiful, a quiet ritual to protect fragile, precious things from envy. Vulnerability like that runs through everything ZÖJ do. Nothing is rehearsed, nothing is fixed after the fact, and once a performance is out in the room it belongs to whoever is listening. That’s how we want to start this year’s Musical Road to WOMEX: with two musicians who make something delicate in front of an audience and then hand it over, so that what happens in Las Palmas will exist only for the people in that room.  ZÖJ means “pair”, and your music is a conversation — kamancheh, voice and drums, largely improvised. For a first-time listener, how would you describe what happens between you on stage? Every ZÖJ performance begins with listening. Before there is sound, there is attention, to each other, to the room, to the audience, to the things that cannot be planned. We don’t approach the stage with a fixed script; we bring our shared musical language and trust. Then we allow the music to reveal itself in the moment. We don’t think of the kamancheh, voice and drums as accompanying one another, more so they’re in conversation. Sometimes they whisper, sometimes they challenge, sometimes they leave space for silence to speak. Our approach to and use of improvisation allows us to be completely present, and that presence becomes something we share with everyone in the room. The audience isn’t only watching the performance; they’re part of shaping its energy. No two concerts are ever the same because no gathering of people is ever the same. Gelareh, you grew up as a girl in Iran where a professional life in music wasn’t an option, and you’ve since made it your whole world across two countries. What in that journey most shapes ZÖJ’s sound? Growing up in Iran, I was surrounded by music. I attended concerts, listened deeply, and was inspired by extraordinary musicians. But as a girl, I also understood from an early age that there were limits on what a musical future could look like for me. Singing publicly as a woman wasn’t a path that was open to me, and that awareness shaped the way I related to music as something precious that had to be protected and pursued with determination. Migrating to Australia gave me the freedom to explore music without those constraints, while carrying with me everything I had learned in Iran. Rather than leaving one world behind for another, ZÖJ lives in the conversation between them. My Iranian heritage, my research into women’s voices in diaspora, and Brian’s openness as an improviser come together in a space where memory meets discovery. I think that’s what most defines our sound: it’s not about choosing between cultures or traditions, but allowing them to meet with honesty, curiosity and deep listening. The Canary Islands are their own crossing of worlds: a Berber Indigenous root, Spanish layers on top, and deep ties to Latin America through centuries of migration. As a duo whose music is about belonging to more than one place, what can that kind of mixed identity mean at this particular moment in history? Mixed identities aren’t exceptions; they’re one of the defining experiences of our time. Most of us carry multiple histories, languages and homes within us. Those intersections aren’t something fragmented, they’re places of creativity and possibility. Music has always travelled more freely than borders allow, and it reminds us that cultures have always been shaped through exchange. The Canary Islands feel like a place where many currents meet. That makes it an especially meaningful setting for WOMEX, because the festival itself celebrates dialogue rather than division. At a time when the world often asks us to choose one identity over another, we’re interested in making music that embraces complexity and connection. Your music is improvisation-based: no two ZÖJ concerts alike, with the audience as a third point of the triangle. In a WOMEX programme full of traditions, what makes that approach distinctly yours, and what do you hope people take from it? We’re deeply rooted in tradition, but we don’t treat tradition as something fixed. The Persian musical language I draw from has always had improvisation at its heart, and we bring that into conversation with contemporary expression, original compositions, and the unique dynamic conversation we’ve developed as a duo. What makes ZÖJ distinctive is that improvisation isn’t a section of the performance, it is the performance. We don’t begin with the intention of reproducing a recording or presenting a definitive version of a piece. We trust the relationship between us, the atmosphere of the room, and the presence of the audience to shape where the music goes. We are creating in real-time, not reciting a learned repertoire. We hope people leave feeling that music can be a living conversation rather than a finished product. If our performance encourages someone to listen more openly, to sound, to silence, to each other, or to their own inner world, then we’ve achieved something meaningful. WOMEX always sparks unexpected meetings. Are there particular artists or showcases you’re looking forward to in Las Palmas? One of the things we love most about festivals is discovering artists we didn’t know we needed to hear. Some of the most memorable musical encounters happen completely by chance. We’re especially looking forward to seeing Nana Benz Du Togo again. We first saw them at WOMADelaide in Australia, and we were so captivated that, while we were standing there watching their set, we bought their record online before the concert had even finished. More broadly, we’re excited by artists who are deeply grounded in their own traditions while remaining open to dialogue and exchange. WOMEX has a remarkable way of bringing those people together, and we’re looking forward as much to the conversations between showcases as the performances themselves. 6Your work asks for deep, patient listening and treats the audience as a collaborator. How does a room of delegates — and an unfamiliar space — shape a ZÖJ set? An unfamiliar space sharpens our listening. We don’t try to make every venue feel the same. We’d rather allow the room to become part of the instrument. The acoustics, the atmosphere, the attention of the audience, all of these influence the music. A room full of delegates can be wonderfully energising because everyone arrives carrying different musical histories. Our hope is that, for a little while, those different backgrounds dissolve into a shared experience of listening. That’s where real connection begins. You’ve spoken about nature feeding directly into your music, the moon, the horizon, the wind in the leaves. What’s your relationship to place and landscape in what you write, and is there anything about a volcanic Atlantic island like Gran Canaria you’re hoping to take in while you’re there? Nature reminds us how to listen. The rhythms of wind, tides, birds, light and silence have always been big influences. We don’t try to imitate nature, but we do try to remember that we’re part of it. We’re looking forward to walking Gran Canaria’s coastline, watching the Atlantic horizon, and spending time with the landscape. Gelareh, your research and your art both centre Iranian women’s voices in diaspora. Is there a message you feel especially compelled to carry through this showcase, at this moment? My work has always been about making space for voices that have too often been unheard. Iranian women have shown extraordinary courage, resilience and creativity, both inside Iran and across the diaspora. Rather than speaking for them, I hope our music creates space where their strength, complexity and humanity can be felt. At a time when many people are displaced by conflict, oppression or circumstance, I hope this showcase reminds us that every migration carries stories, knowledge and beauty, not only pain. Listening deeply to those stories is an act of solidarity. Beyond WOMEX, now that May The Devil’s Ear Be Deaf is out, what’s next for the duo? New writing, touring, collaborations, a direction you haven’t tried yet? We’re excited to let May The Devil’s Ear Be Deaf continue finding its audience through touring and live performance, because that’s where the music keeps evolving. Alongside that, we are always recording new material that continues to explore improvisation, storytelling and the meeting of musical traditions. We’re always open to collaborations with artists from different cultural and artistic backgrounds, particularly where there’s genuine curiosity in communication. If you could write a personal invitation to the people of Las Palmas to come and discover your showcase, what would it say? Dear friends, We would love to meet you through music. If you come to our concert, you won’t hear a performance that has been repeated many times before. You’ll hear something that exists only in that room, on that evening, created together with everyone present. Bring your curiosity. Bring your imagination. Bring your silence as well as your applause. Let’s discover what becomes possible when we truly listen to one another. See you in Las Palmas.   ZÖJ play WOMEX 2026's Official Showcase Selection in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, 21–25 October     PLAYLIST: ZÖJ X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE   The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – ZÖJ appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: ZÖJ 由伊朗裔歌手 Gelareh Pour 与澳大利亚鼓手 Brian O'Dwyer 组成，以卡曼切琴、人声与鼓组为核心，在舞台上完全即兴构建每一次演出。他们的音乐不依赖预先排练或后期修正，而是通过聆听与对话展开，让现场氛围和观众共同塑造作品形态。乐队曾获 2024 年澳大利亚艺术音乐奖实验实践卓越奖，并在加拿大班夫中心以单次现场录音完成第三张专辑《May The Devil's Ear Be Deaf》。专辑标题源自波斯语中用以保护美好事物免受嫉妒的古老短语，呼应了作品中贯穿始终的脆弱感与临场性。Pour 在伊朗成长的经历限制了女性公开演唱的可能，这段历史被她带入音乐，使作品带有鲜明的文化记忆与个人叙事。鼓组与波斯传统乐器之间的碰撞既保留根源，又突破类型边界，每一场演出都因人群与空间的不同而不可复制。

items.excerpt: Old pals Christina Vantzou and Félicia Atkinson reflect on coastal living on their first collaborative album, blending environmental echoes from Rome, Normandy and Hydra with mellow synth, piano, Rhodes, vibraphone, lap steel, gongs and spoken word, pulling us into the sublime. items.body:
Old pals Christina Vantzou and Félicia Atkinson reflect on coastal living on their first collaborative album, blending environmental echoes from Rome, Normandy and Hydra with mellow synth, piano, Rhodes, vibraphone, lap steel, gongs and spoken word, pulling us into the sublime.

The third chapter in RVNG's ongoing "Reflections" series, 'Water Poems' crystallises a creative relationship that began way back in 2009. Vantzou and Atkinson have performed together before, most notably in 2019 at Philharmonie de Paris, but this is the first time the duo have made a record together. Both artists live by the sea, Atkinson in Normandy on the French coast, and Vantzou in Greece, using that shared experience to power a series of hazy dream sequences filled with subtle gestures. "The sea was not taken as a monolithic postcard," Atkinson explains. "But more of a person; an energy, a mystery, a complex character we face everyday, as human beings living by the sea."

Indeed, the esoteric energy of the sea - its tides, force, majesty and hypnotic, mystical pull, is captured by the duo's eddy of electroacoustic treatments and bespoke natural soundscapes. They recorded the material in a factory on the island of Hydra in Greece, at Villa Medici in Rome and at home in their respective studios, adding expressive environmental recordings from Delphi and the Eftalou Hot Springs. The record plays like a single, hazed thought, ebbing and flowing through the same shallow waters. Words emerge and disappear into carefully processed sounds at first, before forming sentences and whole thoughts on the second side. "How can a body swim," Atkinson mouthes. "How can a person dream?"

Gorgeously, quietly seductive gear from two of the very best at this sort of thing, one to file next to Meitei's sublime 'Sen'nyū (泉涌)' from last year - recline and drift into it.
items._genre: ambient / experimental / electroacoustic / field recording / drone
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是两位长期合作的艺术家首次以双人组合形式推出的作品，灵感源于她们各自在海边的生活经验。录音素材取自希腊伊兹拉岛上的工厂、罗马美第奇别墅以及各自家中，并加入德尔斐和埃夫塔卢温泉的环境录音。音乐以合成器、钢琴、电钢、颤音琴、钢棒吉他和锣等乐器为基础，配合人声念白与环境声，营造出如潮汐般缓慢流动的声响景观。人声在开头部分隐没于处理过的声音中，随后逐渐清晰，形成完整的语句和思绪。专辑通过细腻的声音编排捕捉海洋的神秘与能量，而非将其呈现为单一的明信片式意象，在电声处理与自然声响之间形成持续的对话。作为RVNG厂牌Reflections系列的第三部，作品在氛围音乐与实验声响之间保持了高度的统一性和沉浸感。

items.body:
STROOM fills in a gap on the timeline, excavating vital experiments made in Cologne in the wake of the cult 'Novaya Scena' compilation by Svitlana Nianio, Michael Springer, Guido Erfen, Soloveyka, Yewgeny Taran and Wolfram Burgtorf.

Back in 1993, a bizarre 20-track compilation appeared from Cologne's musical fringe. The idea for the set had come from artist and producer Erfen and sound engineer and percussionist Springer, two close friends who, taking advantage of cheap rent and disused buildings, put on regular events and established a recording studio in their neighborhood, off the beaten track. Erfen was a dedicated tape trader and had received a transmission from Kharkiv's Novaya Scena rock club that arrived with an essay and music from three local bands. At this time, Ukraine was still under Soviet rule and the music fascinated the two friends, shining a spotlight on a part of the world they were completely unfamiliar with. When singer and keyboardist Soloveyka visited cologne a year later, she handed Erfan more tantalizing music, inspiring him to make his own pilgrimage to Ukraine to investigate further. The research resulted in the 'Novaya Scene' CD, a set of tracks recorded between 1986 and 1992 that muddled prog with new wave, punk, folk and avant-garde rock. It was released on Hamburg's What's So Funny About label and was supposed to have a sequel.

That's where 'Aftermath and Transitions' comes in. Following the release of 'Novaya Scena', Erfen and Springer set up a series of sessions at their studio, inviting some of the Ukrainian artists to record with them. It's this period that resulted in Svitlana Nianio's 'Transilvania Smile' soundtrack that was properly released for the first time on Muscat sublabel Shukai in 2023. Nianio had been a member of Cukor Bila Smerť (the band who'd provided the stylistic anchor for 'Novaya Scena') and took the opportunity to launch her solo career, with Springer working as engineer. And there was more material from those sessions that Springer held back: the compilation's first four tracks are collaborations between Nianio, Springer, Taran and Springer's good friend Burgtorf. Opener 'Fake' was almost finished when Nianio showed up at the studio with her Casio in tow, so Springer plugged her in and she ended up lavishing the beat with vocals in Ukrainian and oddball keyboard vamps. The other three tracks were a little more organic, improvised in the studio while the artists got familiar with one another - there's the decelerated reggae experiment 'ManySpace', the instrumental groover 'Quiet Place' and best of all 'Політ Світляки', a wiry percussive jam that's not aged a day.

Erfen joins in on the ace exotica-tinged 'Whispering Walls' and 'Tired River', tracks from the group's final session in 1995. Nianio and Taran were planning to renew their visas and return to Cologne to record more, but it never happened - the recordings were shelved and the artists went about their lives independently. Then there's the three Solar tracks recorded by Soloveyka and Burgtorf who struck up a friendship after meeting at Springer's studio. Singing in Russian and English, Soloveyka breathes cabaret energy over Burgtorf's jerky, sample-heavy ethno-groove productions. And it's left to Taran to finish things off, with a "1996 Version" of his 'Death and the Bachelor' track that features none other than Nianio on keys. Phew. It's a brilliant set, really - not just one for STROOM obsessives, it'll speak to anyone whose interest in the Ukrainian underground was piqued by 'Transilvania Smile' or Muscut's ace Cukor Bila Smerť anthology.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了1994至1996年间乌克兰音乐人在科隆留下的录音，源于《新场景》之后埃尔芬与斯普林格组织的工作室合作。尼阿尼奥带着卡西欧键盘加入的开篇曲，在节拍上叠加乌克兰语人声与怪诞键盘；其余曲目多为即兴，包括减速雷鬼实验、器乐律动和一首打击乐质感鲜明的作品。埃尔芬参与的两首带有异国情调，来自1995年最后一次集体录音。这些母带一度被搁置，如今补全了乌克兰地下场景在西欧的一段重要轨迹。

items.body:
Dreader than dread dub vapors from Ghost Dubs, in a lineage stretching from Dadawah to Burial Mix, Vainqueur to Resilent, Pole to Rod Modelll...​

Toiling in Berlin’s deep seam of abstract dub practice that scrolls back to Rhythm & Sound’s earliest via Pole’s dusty convections and Chain Reaction's fritzed mutations; Ghost Dubs embodies the art of dub as method with a strong haul of dematerialised, sludgy tramplers operating close to the scuzzy heart of Kevin Martin, aka The Bug. Uncompromisingly in-the-zone and dank as a bong, the dozen cuts get right under the skin, up-the-pharynx, with an intoxicatingly sedated and hallucinatory quality that impresses murky, vaporous patterns on the back of blunted eyelids and may possibly raise knees to its slompy skank and imaginary physics. 

Of course, the sound is rooted in the innovative, half century-old traditions of Jamaican dub, as established by King Tubby and Lee “Scratch” Perry, and developed by the likes of Scientist or Mad Professor. But Ghost Dubs picks it up at the point where it diffused into techno and noise during the ‘90s, taking that sound as a jump-off into his microcosm of granular, atomised atmospheric disintegration that nevertheless holds to a steady ballast of scoop-worrying sub-bass tremors. No doubt anyone who’s followed the devolution of this sound outside Jamaica, from NYC illbient to Berlin dub techno, will recognise his hands-on-desk tekkerz ushering the sound into oblique new spaces with a canny sense of proprioception that locates it somewhere in fissure between classic and contemporary soundspheres.

From the caustic attrition of ‘Chemical’, thru the inverted mulch of ‘Dub Lobotomy’, to the sensuous but elephantine trample of ‘Hot Wired’ and tumescent swell of ‘Circles Lines’ ,Ghost Dubs leaves his clammy fingerprint on every cut. Some are primed to bend your Clarks, as with the bilgy step of ‘The Regulator’, and airborne skank of ‘Thin Line’, and the harness-tugging pressure of ‘Dub Battle’, but they’re all held in check with a overarching slowness that gels the 12 tracks as a proper end-to-end listen in the manner of Pole’s early albums with a deeply reliable robustness and temper that stakes it out as arguably canonic tackle.
items._genre: dub / dub techno / ambient / experimental / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将牙买加dub传统引入柏林抽象电子声景，在King Tubby与Rhythm & Sound的脉络中开辟出颗粒化、雾化的新维度。十二首作品以缓慢而沉重的节奏铺展，sub-bass震颤与泥泞质感贯穿始终，既保留dub的松弛律动，又融入techno的机械脉冲与noise的侵蚀性。乐评强调其声音如同在眼睑内侧留下模糊蒸汽般的图案，兼具催眠感与幻觉特质，同时以精准的混音手法在经典与当代之间找到独特位置。从《Chemical》的腐蚀性磨损到《Dub Lobotomy》的倒置腐殖质层，每首曲目都带有鲜明的个人印记，整体连贯性堪比Pole早期专辑，被视为该领域具有经典潜力的作品。

items.body:
Carrier winds the rhythmic tension to breaking point on his 4th self-released 12”, flexing fine-tuned muscle memory and inch-tight production in acres of negative space across a trio of soundsystem phantoms that dance in the long shadow of D&B and broken beat science. Huge tip FFO Autechre, Burial, Photek, T++.

Now three years into a generational run of inspirational plates - including an AOTY ’25 with ‘Rhythm Immortal’ for Modern Love - Carrier’s core sense of discipline and restraint continues to yield peerless reward on ‘Thresholds’. A lifetime’s love of, and immersion in, fwd UK dance musics has prompted him to chase a particular dragon of syncopated swerve and cavernous psychoacoustics to logical, next-level depths diffusing that dread pressure with an adroit, tendon-twitching precision and tactility.

Carrier has been instrumental in reminding ravers what was lost when D&B went stadium and pop-chart scale over the past decades, daring to run against the grain, trust his instincts, to return a sense of mystery and bold experimentalism to what was once a thrilling paradigm. This new trio of cuts eke exquisite nuance from tweaked fundamentals, swivelling 2-step off the bone into smoky hall-of-mirrors reflections of ‘Cure’, and specialising in a razor’s edge, toes-off-the-ground sorcery in a recursive, wraithlike zinger, ‘Scout’ that dips to the sexiest, tongue-tip breakdown, beside the tantric, anticipatory chicanery of ‘Black Channels’ which finishes us off with an all-tension-no-release weapon for the ages.

items._cn_summary: Carrier在第四张自主发行的十二寸黑胶中，将节奏张力推向极限，以极简空间承载精密制作，三首作品在鼓打贝斯与碎拍科学的阴影下呈现幽灵般的声响幻象。他延续了近年备受赞誉的创作脉络，以克制与纪律重构英国舞曲中失落的实验精神，避开主流化后的宏大与流行化，转而探索切分摆动与深邃心理声学的逻辑深度。曲目在扭曲的基础元素中提取细腻变化，将两步节拍剥离为烟雾弥漫的镜厅反射，同时以剃刀边缘般的轻盈感营造出悬空般的魔法时刻，并在持续紧绷而不释放的结构中完成收束。整体上，这张作品展现了Carrier对节奏细节的敏锐掌控，以及在地下电子语境中重新注入神秘感与大胆实验性的能力。

items.excerpt: Joining the 4AD roster, NYC avant-rock four piece YHWH Nailgun unload an 11-minute clip of pure math-punk artillery, all demon-possessed vocals, screaming organs, angular riffs and byzantine rhythms. Think U.S. Maple, Battles, Captain Beefheart, Pere Ubu and Still House Plants blended with 'Scum'-era Napalm Death and you'll have some idea. items.body:
Joining the 4AD roster, NYC avant-rock four piece YHWH Nailgun unload an 11-minute clip of pure math-punk artillery, all demon-possessed vocals, screaming organs, angular riffs and byzantine rhythms. Think U.S. Maple, Battles, Captain Beefheart, Pere Ubu and Still House Plants blended with 'Scum'-era Napalm Death and you'll have some idea.

Deployed only moments after Drake dropped not one but three bloated sets of playlist-ready mall pop, 'Magazine' arrives like a cool breeze during a heatwave. See, it's common sense in the AI era to feed the algorithms more, not less, increasing your chances to snag that illusive viral hit by relying on pure volume. Not hampered by the limitations of the format (remember, the "classic album" was only 40-odd minutes because vinyl demanded it), artists and labels have been hedging their bets, packing records with collaborations, remixes and undeveloped ideas in the hope that one of them might end up getting even half the traction of AFX's seemingly throwaway 'QKThr'. YHWH Nailgun laugh in the face of this logic, not just challenging 2026's idea of what an album should be, but 1966's, too. If you thought '45 Pounds' was lean, 'Magazine' trims even more aesthetic fat, cooking down the meat of jazz fusion, prog, noise rock, post-punk and grindcore like it's Wagyu, searing it off and providing just an umami-rich shaving to taste.

The whole process is surprising because so many of YHWH Nailgun's references were already bloated. The prog rock era was when the double album became almost commonplace; 'Magazine' meanwhile could quite easily be crammed onto a 7" at 45RPM. And yet, they've only increased in power since last year. Opener 'Ghost of Love' does more in a minute-and-a-half than most tracks do in three or four times the duration, spinning Jack Tobias' carnivalesque, Farfisa-like synths around Sam Pickard's pliant drums like matted spiderwebs, but leaving just enough room for Zack Borzone's no-wave shouts and Saguiv Rosenstock's hacking fragments of melody. 'Stillness Blues' is shorter still and somehow packs even more in, assembling screamo brickwork over industrial strength bass rasps using Pickard's clattery start-stop patterns as the mortar. It's hard to say this stuff's exhausting - it's over before you've even really come to grips with it - but YHWH Nailgun have a way of drawing you back in, again and again, just to try and catch a whiff of what's actually going on. 

There's the Radiohead-like moan of 'Innocent Sigh', the Eli Keszler-does-Pere Ubu intensity of the minute-long 'Ballerina' and the title track, 35 seconds of breakneck beats, bleeps and shouted phrases that rudely cuts off before it's even had the chance to fully extend its claws. It's a shocker, an eccentric, hyper skillful, deeply original blur of influences and innovation that really does remind us just how punchy rock music can be.
items._genre: avant-rock / math-punk / noise rock / post-punk / grindcore
items._cn_summary: YHWH Nailgun的《Magazine》以不到十一分钟的总长呈现极高密度的实验摇滚冲击，将爵士融合、前卫摇滚、噪音摇滚、后朋克与碾核元素压缩至极端精炼的片段中。恶魔附体般的人声、尖叫风琴、棱角分明的吉他线条与繁复节奏交织，每首曲目短促而饱满，如开篇曲仅九十秒便完成多重动态转换，标题曲更以三十五秒的急速节拍与喊叫戛然而止。作品刻意对抗流媒体时代以数量博取关注的逻辑，拒绝冗长铺陈，在极短篇幅内塞入大量声响细节与结构突变。乐评特别指出其参考了U.S. Maple、Battles、Captain Beefheart、Pere Ubu及早期Napalm Death等对象，但最终形成高度原创的融合面貌，既保留噪音摇滚的粗粝，又具备前卫作曲般的控制力，值得反复聆听以捕捉其中层叠的细节。

items.body:
One of the UK’s most distinctive filmmakers returns to the sea, replete with his original synth score - as on ‘Bait’ and ‘Enys Men’ - but notably damper, deeply blue; surely evoking fellow Cornish native AFX’s ‘SAW II’, BoC interludes, Mordant Music, classic folk horror OSTs.

Centred around the tale of a trawler that returns, sans crew, to a Cornish harbour years after it was thought lost, ‘The Rose Of Nevada’ typically draws on what Mark Jenkin knows best - the people, places and metaphysics of the Atlantic peninsula - whilst ideally emphasising the atmosphere with his special ingredient score. His palette of tape-smudged analog synths feels especially washed out and suggestive of his subject in its briny tone and oceanic scale, which evidently works a treat as a discrete work in its own right, severed from imagery. 

There’s possibly a Kernewek word for “hiraeth”, or “sehnsucht” - a sense of longing, nostalgia - that we’re not aware of, but may perfectly fit the feeling of Jenkin’s music here. Sea-legged loops and sustained drones colour the air with a palpable melancholy in passage from the bittersweet tang of ‘Kneebone Barton’, as used on the trailer, and throughout the album’s patches of decaying wheeze, staining the surface like rust or efflorescence on weathered coves. 

And in the day-dreamiest sense it all fades in/out of consciousness with a perfectly ghostly wow and flutter, as leaching from ‘Through The Gaps’ parts into the slurred whorl of ‘What’s Your Name,’ ephemeral concrète of ‘Look At It’, and final folksy shuffle off into the horizon with ‘Rose of Nevada.’ Here’s looking forward to the film.
items._genre: ambient / electronic / drone / film score / folk horror
items._cn_summary: 这张原声专辑围绕一艘失踪拖网渔船归来的故事展开，以磁带模糊的模拟合成器营造潮湿深蓝的海洋氛围，带有康沃尔地方性的怀旧与乡愁。音乐在持续低音、漂移循环和衰减的喘息声之间铺展，类似AFX早期氛围作品与民间恐怖配乐的交汇。作为独立于影像的听觉作品，它通过缓慢淡入淡出的方式组织意识流，从苦涩微甜的段落过渡到模糊旋转的声响，最终以民谣式律动收束。其将电影配乐、氛围电子与地方民间记忆融合的路径，使声音本身成为叙事与情绪的主体。

items.body:
Swedish jazz icon Christer Bothén returns to Black Truffle backed by Ghosted's Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling and Andreas Werliin, playing bass clarinet and donso n’goni over the trio's signature kraut-jazz grooves. Hypnotic, trance-inducing biz FFO Natural Information Society, Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society', Jon Hassell, The Necks.

If you're up on your Swedish jazz, there's no way you won't have stumbled across multi-instrumentalist Bothén. He's still best known for palling around with Don Cherry when the jazz great moved to Scandinavia, even teaching him how to play the donso n'goni, a sacred "hunter's harp" from the Wassoulou region in West Africa that Bothén had picked up when he was in Mali. And he's continued to perform with various local artists and outfits, conspicuously appearing on Ghosted's 2022 debut album just mere moments before Ambarchi's Black Truffle imprint re-issued his lost Afro-fusion classic album 'Trancedance'. Last year, Bothén finally issued his first solo n'goni album and now he's back on Black Truffle with this fleshed-out collaboration with the Ghosted crew, leading Ambarchi's Leslie-cab guitar drones, Berthling's bass and Werliin's drums.

Berthling and Werliin take the lead at first on the title track, hammering out a rotating groove before Bothén lets rip on bass clarinet. And playing a side role, Ambarchi might have the most important presence, using his signature phased, organ-like tones to provide anchoring drones for Bothén's spirited improvisations. He's even more pivotal on 'Antigorite', playing cascading staccato notes over those Leslie moans and creating an rhythmelodic foil for the other three players' more traditional interplay. But it's when Bothén plays the n'ghoni that the album really hits its stride; on 'Lizardite', those buzzing tones offset Ambarchi's crystalline twangs, filling in for Werliin's imposing basslines. It's the moment where everything else just drops into place, creating a structural crescendo before the album careers into darkness on the brilliantly moody closer 'Chrysotile'.
items._genre: experimental jazz / world fusion / kraut-jazz / drone
items._cn_summary: 瑞典爵士老将Christer Bothén与Ghosted乐队成员合作，在Black Truffle旗下推出这张融合爵士与西非传统乐器的专辑。Bothén演奏低音单簧管和donso n'goni，Ambarchi以标志性的Leslie风琴式吉他嗡鸣提供持续音层，Berthling与Werliin的节奏组则构筑旋转式律动。开篇曲以贝斯和鼓的循环动机引入，随后单簧管即兴切入；在《Antigorite》中，Ambarchi的颗粒状分解音符与低鸣管风琴音色形成节奏旋律对位。当Bothén在《Lizardite》中弹起n'goni时，其嗡鸣质感与Ambarchi的清脆拨弦交织，替代贝斯线条，推动专辑走向结构性的高潮，最终坠入阴郁的收尾曲《Chrysotile》。整张专辑在催眠式重复与即兴张力之间取得平衡，展现了传统乐器与实验爵士语汇的有机融合。

items.body:
In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to marvel at one of the finest examples of loop-based electronic music typical of the early noughties.

Taking what reads like a pretty austere set of ingredients, Jelinek's technique revolves around a trio of elements which consist of second long cuts of 1960's-70's jazz recordings, the loop-finding modulation wheel (do your homework!) and the Moiré effect; albeit rendered in the acoustic as opposed to the image and spectral domains.

If all this sounds a bit academic, be assured that on record it is anything but; as crumbling edifices of mealy rhythms slowly pulse into life and swirl around your head like snow storms clashing with a dust devil. Taking sediments of fathom deep static then skimming the best stuff from the top, Jelinek opens through the dampened echoes of 'Moiré (piano & organ)' wherein a slow-motion thrum of spiraling clicks, rustles and analogue tones conspire to give the impression of recondite perspectives that extend well beyond the constituent elements.

Elsewhere, 'Rocky in the Video Age' instills a gratuitously optimistic blush to the aquatic micro-sound ebb, 'Moiré (Strings)' is a perfect companion to Basinski's disintegrating tape archive, whilst 'Them, Their' represents an aural crease so sleight you can only catch its distinctive gleam from the corner of your eye.
items._cn_summary: Jan Jelinek 的这张经典专辑以1960至70年代爵士录音的秒级切片为素材，通过循环调制与波纹效应构建出独特的声响织体。不同于学院派概念的枯燥，音乐呈现出细碎节奏缓慢脉动的生动质感，仿佛尘埃般的声音颗粒在空间中旋转、碰撞。开篇曲以阻尼回声、螺旋式咔嗒声与模拟音调营造出深邃的聆听纵深；后续曲目则分别注入乐观光泽、与Basinski式消解磁带美学呼应的弦乐切片，以及近乎不可捕捉的微妙褶皱。整张专辑在极简素材中提炼出丰富的听觉层次，是早期零年代循环电子音乐的典范之作。

items.body:
Our Darkness descends upon Dark Entries with a reissue of Anne Clark’s epochal proto-house masterpiece from 1984.

"As a young poet, Clark found herself drawn to London’s emerging punk scene. She became acquainted with Psychic TV affiliate David Harrow, with whom she would collaborate on 1983’s Changing Places and 1984’s Joined Up Writing. “Our Darkness,” off the latter album, was released as a single on Ink Records that same year, and became an underground club hit. It’s a singular piece of music: Clark’s lyrics, delivered with equal parts muscular confidence and unease, speak of urban alienation and heartbreak, while Harrow’s production pummels the listener with hydraulic beats and gloom-laced arpeggios. The song’s spirit would prove influential on both the early Chicago house and Detroit techno scenes, where mechanistic funk and existential despair could catalyse dancefloor mayhem.

This reissue offers three versions of “Our Darkness”: the original 12” remix, the Razormaid mix, and a previously unreleased dub version uncovered by David Harrow. Also included is the extended mix of “Sleeper in Metropolis,” another dancefloor hit of Clark’s, as well as the elegiac “Poem for a Nuclear Romance.”

“Our Darkness” channels timeless longing and contemporary dismay, a classic overdue for a little light shed upon it."
items._cn_summary: Anne Clark 1984年的经典单曲“Our Darkness”以再版形式重现，收录原版12寸混音、Razormaid混音、David Harrow发掘的未发行dub版本，并附上另一首舞池金曲“Sleeper in Metropolis”的加长混音及“Poem for a Nuclear Romance”。Clark以兼具力量与不安的诗歌朗诵，讲述都市疏离与心碎；Harrow的制作则以液压般的节拍和阴郁琶音构筑机械感与绝望感并存的声响空间。这首作品对早期芝加哥house与底特律techno场景产生深远影响，将机制化的律动与存在主义式的压抑转化为舞池中的颠覆性能量。再版让这首影响深远的暗黑舞曲重见天日，也呈现了其多版本的面貌与历史脉络。

items.body:
One of electronic music's most influential recordings, back in circulation.

Most readers of these pages will know the story, but to indulge you with a recap, Gottsching was part of electronic krautrock heroes Ash Ra Tempel and in 1981, off the back of a Klaus Schulze tour, sat down one evening and dropped a continuous piece of music which would uncannily imagine the arc of dance music for a quarter of a century.

Early adopters in the Chicago and Detroit warehouses and mediterranean pleasure palaces must have thrilled to the balanced and continuous surging flow of the hour long piece - even over two sides the mix is perfect for building a club atmosphere and suggesting avenues for mixing, whilst using merely two chords throughout. the minimalism offsets the percussive splendour perfectly - several years later the tune was rediscovered and co-opted into the huge italo house smash Sueno Latino, which cemented its foundation in the burgeoning balearic scene of the time and proceeded through several spells of rapturous revival throughout the nineties, not least when figures like Carl Craig and Basic Channel issued their own radically different reshapes and remakes of the piece.

Very satisfying then to have this Gottsching sanctioned edition, where the game might truly be said to have begun in earnest. As they say on the august walls of the Hardwax emporium - buy or die.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国音乐家曼努埃尔·格特辛格于1981年某次晚间即兴中录制的连续长篇电子作品。全曲时长约一小时，仅用两个和弦贯穿，以缓慢推进的脉冲、重复的合成器音型和极简的打击层次，构造出持续涌动的空间感。乐评认为，它仿佛预见了此后二十五年舞曲音乐的发展轨迹；芝加哥、底特律的仓库派对与地中海俱乐部场景中的早期采纳者，都曾为其均衡而绵长的流动感所吸引。作品后来被改编为意大利浩室名曲，并经由卡尔·克雷格和基本频道等人物以截然不同的方式重混，进一步奠定其在巴利阿里场景和九十年代多次复兴中的根基。此次再版由格特辛格本人认可，被视为这段历史真正展开的起点。

items.body:
On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell.

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge formative passions for microtonal just intonation - as seeded in Terry Riley’s ‘Shri Camel’ - and slippery syncopation to the fullest. Half solo, proper, and half peppered with percussion by regular spar, Matt Davies, it follows his nose for open frontiers of alternative tunings and wonky meter with the blend of low key modesty and prism-pushing tekkerz that have long endeared his work to lovers of lower case experimental music. 

Sweetly balanced between timeless, folk-soul-wise and futurist sensibilities, the half hour suite knits hyaline synths and rippling gamelan metallophonics with clarinet and guitar in lissom, sloshing shapes that effortlessly seduce, rather than demand, the listener’s attention. In particular we are drawn to the bits in duo with Davies, floating sublime ideas in the dreamlike, inverted dub architexture of ‘Ion’, settling on mind like a strangely bucolic Incus work on ’Sundry’, and thru the exquisite, tip-toed rhythms of ‘Ecstatic’, to a trippier, bittersweet type of ante-chamber music on ‘Fret (Hear)’.

He’s also deeply charming when left to his own devices. Ambient opener ‘Billow’ calls to mind the tenderness of Cotton Goods works, and ‘Knead’ chases a certain geist of Irdial or Plaid-esque gamelantronica into the sublime title tune, while ‘Prism’ most beautifully ties all his interests in a melting dream sequence which he caps with the harmonic nightlight glow of ‘Column’.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以另类调弦和微音程纯律为核心，结合滑动的切分节奏，营造出轻柔而专注的聆听体验。Barley与打击乐手Matt Davies的合作占据半数曲目，在《Ion》《Sundry》《Ecstatic》中呈现梦幻般的倒置混响建筑和精致踮脚般的节奏。独奏部分如《Billow》《Knead》《Prism》则展现环境化的甘美兰电子声响与旋律夜光。整体介于民谣般的温情与未来主义之间，融合合成器、金属打击、单簧管与吉他，形成一种不刻意吸引却自然沉浸的室内乐质感。

items.excerpt: Munich’s modern art gallery Museum Brandhorst field wide ranging responses to an exhibit of works and concerts focussed on the works of John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg and Cy Twombly, ranging from the sound poetry of Sofia Biazzi; to the sublime levitations of Maria Margolina; avant ambient pop of water lily; the pulsating technoid attack of focus baby; andCaroline Kretschmer’s subaquatic intrigue. “Museum Brandhorst has invited Sound and Experiment to create a ser
items.body:
Munich’s modern art gallery Museum Brandhorst field wide ranging responses to an exhibit of works and concerts focussed on the works of John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg and Cy Twombly, ranging from the sound poetry of Sofia Biazzi; to the sublime levitations of Maria Margolina; avant ambient pop of water lily; the pulsating technoid attack of focus baby; andCaroline Kretschmer’s subaquatic intrigue.

“Museum Brandhorst has invited Sound and Experiment to create a series of performances, audio works, and concerts in relation to the exhibition Fünf Freunde: John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg, Cy Twombly. The event took place on June 27, 2025, as part of the Junge Nacht and the opening night of the annual Kunstareal Fest in Munich. The program featured newly produced pieces by Sound and Experiment participants Sofian Biazzi, Ilinca Fechete, focus baby, Daniel Gianfranceschi, Bruno Haas, Caroline Kretschmer, Bradley Leonard, Camilla Metelka, Maria Margolina, rosi and water lily. 

In a preparatory, biweekly seminar, discussions addressed conditions such as spectrotemporal displays, sharing time and frequency domains with different sound pieces simultaneously, and eventual performance constellations. An additional point of departure was a close reading of the indirect role of American artist David Tudor in some of the positions exhibited in Fünf Freunde, the function of the organization E.A.T. (Experiments in Art and Technology), and auditory scene analysis and synthesis in general.

The pieces featured on this CD are related to the presented performances, yet newly produced and with the audio CD format in mind.”
items._genre: experimental / sound poetry / ambient / electronic / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是慕尼黑现代美术馆Brandhorst围绕约翰·凯奇、默斯·坎宁安等五位艺术家展览所策划的声音项目成果，收录了多位参与者的全新录音室作品。内容从索菲亚·比亚齐的声音诗，到玛丽亚·马尔戈利娜的悬浮感氛围，再到水百合的前卫环境流行、focus baby的脉冲式电子攻击，以及卡罗琳·克雷奇默的水下神秘声响，风格跨度极大。作品在筹备过程中经过双周研讨，探讨了频谱时间展示、多声部时间与频率域共享、以及听觉场景分析等概念，并以CD格式重新构思制作。整体上呈现出一种以声音装置思维驱动的策展式合辑，兼顾实验性、空间感与多元融合，适合关注当代声音艺术与前卫音乐的听众。

items.body:
An iconic album originally brought to life via Sweden's peerless iDEAL Recordings, Kali Malone’s 'The Sacrificial Code’ is a major work featuring almost two hours of concentrated, creeping organ pieces aligned to non traditional intonation/tuning systems. It's a stunning realisation of ideas borne out of academic and conceptual rigour, with a perception-altering quality that encourages exploration without a preordained endpoint.

The Sacrificial Code’ takes a more surgical approach to the methods first explored on last year’s ‘Organ Dirges 2016 - 2017’. Over the course of three parts performed on three different organs, Malone’s minimalist process captures a jarring precision of closeness, both on the level of the materiality of the sounds and on the level of composition.The recordings here involved careful close miking of the pipe organ in such a way as to eliminate environmental identifiers as far as possible - essentially removing the large hall reverb so inextricably linked to the instrument. The pieces were then further compositionally stripped of gestural adornments and spontaneous expressive impulse -  an approach that flows against the grain of the prevailing musical hegemony, where sound is so often manipulated, and composition often steeped in self indulgence. It echoes Steve Reich’s sentiment “..by voluntarily giving up the freedom to do whatever momentarily comes to mind, we are, as a result, free of all that momentarily comes to mind.”

With its slow, purified and seemingly austere qualities ‘The Sacrificial Code’ guides us through an almost trance-inducing process where we become vulnerable receptors for every slight movement, where every miniature shift in sound becomes magnified through stillness. As such, it’s a uniquely satisfying exercise in transcendence through self restraint and by this point inarguably a modern classic.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以近两小时的管风琴作品构成，采用非传统调音与律制，在极简主义框架下探索声音的物质性。录音通过近距离拾音刻意消除教堂大厅的混响，使管风琴的机械细节与音色纹理变得异常清晰；作曲层面则剥离了装饰性乐句与即兴冲动，仅保留缓慢、纯净、近乎严苛的声音演进。三部分分别在不同管风琴上录制，形成一种高度专注的聆听体验，细微的音高变化与泛音在静止中被放大，引导听者进入近乎催眠的状态。作品延续了作曲家对学院派概念与结构控制的兴趣，同时以自我约束的方式获得感知层面的解放，被评论视为当代实验音乐中的一部重要作品。

items.body:
Not the birth of acid house, but a thrilling piece of synth raga set to brisk disco beats, Bollywood soundtrack composer Charanjit Singh’s ’82 LP is simply a landmark in its own right, and a proper ‘floor-filler to boot.

Since its first reissue in 2010, Singh’s cult, early use of the TB-303 on driving machine beats has been erroneously hailed the birth of acid house. OK the formula is there, but Chris Carter’s ‘Spaces Between’ (1980) and his CTI jam ‘Dancing Ghosts’ got there a couple of years before Singh, at the very least, and neither really inform the genius of Phuture and co a few years later. In any event, ‘Synthesizing: Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’ is just an incredibly fruity boost to any club, revolving 10 hypnotic, pulsating jams closer to early Irdial (say, Aqua Regia’s ‘Hot Love’) than owt from the Chi. 

Taking a minute away from knocking out Bollywood scores and leading his wedding band covering popular songs, Singh would land upon a stroke of genius with ‘Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’, finding the sweetspot between prevailing hi-NRG disco and millennia of raga traditions that patently transcended the sum of their parts more than 40 years later. It sounds very much of its time, rather than the stripped back linearity of later acid house, evidenced in the florid keyboard urges of ‘Raga Bhupali’, transposing a steamy sort of club canter to somewhere even more humid.

A real club evergreen, suck it and see.
items._cn_summary: Charanjit Singh 在宝莱坞配乐与婚礼乐队工作之余，用 TB-303 和合成器将印度拉格旋律嵌入高速迪斯科节拍，录制出这张 1982 年的俱乐部唱片。十首曲目以循环脉动的方式推进，键盘装饰繁复，氛围比后来的 acid house 更湿润，也更接近当时 hi-NRG 舞曲的质感。乐评指出它常被误认为 acid house 的起源，但更应被视作独立的里程碑；其价值在于拉格传统与舞池律动之间找到的独特交汇点，而非对芝加哥后辈的直接启发。作为舞池常青曲目，它至今仍能提供强烈的现场能量，同时保留着鲜明的时代印记。

items.body:
Billed as a sequel to 2024's 'Something in the Room She Moves', 'Materia' augments and extends Julia Holter's unique vision, chopping and screwing the Hildegard von Bingen-inspired title track and swaddling it with more psychotropic chamber pop experiments. Dizzier and more surreal than the original album, it might be even more dazzling - properly vital FFO Mabe Fratti, Jessica Pratt, ANOHNI or Jenny Hval.

Ever since we got snagged by 2011's AOTY 'Tragedy', we've been captivated by her particular fusion of baroque pop, high drama and groggy minimalism - elements that inevitably arrive tied together with an air of effortless avant charm. And she's only refined her approach over the years, delivering a Laurel Canyon-via-Dusseldorf labyrinth of sophisticated juxtapositions on her last album. It was clearly so knotty, in fact, that Holter felt the need to revisit its serene centerpiece 'Materia', rolling out two new versions that triggered this heady, casually brilliant companion album. The rework that started it all, 'Materia 2', isn't some George Lucas affair, either; Holter goes back to the chilly original and genuinely reimagines it, adding a decelerated hypnagogic drum machine pulse that's one part AFX's 'Selected Ambient Works Volume II' and one part Antena's perennial classic 'Camino del Sol'. Holter never loses sight of the initial mystical inspiration, retaining the celestial ecstasy with Laswell-style fretless electric bass and soaring keys as she sings "My heart is loud."

The third version of 'Materia' is more of a bonus track (a self-conscious homage to those mysterious unlisted extras that often appeared on CDs) and finds the divine in languidness, pulling down the tempo and letting the words and harmonies sound out into the empty, reverberant space. But both of these tracks work more like anchors for what's essentially a brand new album; the jerky, 'Hounds of Love'-esque opener 'The Laugh is in the Eyes' is already one of Holter's most inviting, lavish productions. Led by its cannily sculpted rhythm section at first, it flourishes when Holter lets the aesthetic tumult disappear altogether, singing out coolly over weightless pads. And that AFX-cum-Antena influence isn't relegated to the titular redux. The album's lead single 'Fantasy' is an art-pop miracle that sounds as if she's daydreaming over a demo that was passed between Rephlex and Les Disques du Crepuscule before it was lost in the mail some time in the early '90s. It doesn't rest on its laurels either, exploding outwards and somehow integrating tape saturated Walker Brothers-esque psych pop before snapping right back into the groove.

There's a pause for breath on the brief, voice-led 'Clepsydra' before Holter dives headfirst into the extended 'My Twin', the track where she pinched the lead riff she used on 'Fantasy'. When we hear that familiar refrain emerge from near silence, played on an orchestra of broken music boxes and mussed with disorienting pitch and tape delay effects, it's as if we're being scrubbed through someone else's dream. It's one of those tracks that reaffirms why Holter's so good at what she does, composed from a tangled web of ideas and references and sounding somehow effortless at the same time. 'Materia' is Holter at her most whimsical - and most vital.
items._genre: art pop / experimental / avant-garde / electronic / chamber pop
items._cn_summary: Julia Holter的《Materia》作为《Something in the Room She Moves》的续作，对同名曲进行减速与拼贴式重制，并扩展为迷幻室内流行实验。新版本加入催眠鼓机脉冲，融合AFX式氛围电子与Antena式合成器流行，同时保留希尔德加德·冯·宾根启发的神秘主义内核。专辑还包含《The Laugh is in the Eyes》和《Fantasy》等新作，前者以精巧节奏与空灵人声营造奢华艺术流行，后者则交织早期电子舞曲与Walker Brothers式迷幻流行。整体在巴洛克流行、高戏剧性与慵懒极简之间游走，通过破损音乐盒音色、磁带延迟和空间混响构建出独特的声响拼贴，既延续了她一贯的先锋气质，又在细节上实现了更具沉浸感的再创造。

items.body:
The eminently watchable Accidental Meetings introduce extended family member, Lovely Dave, with a real guess-again mixtape (the first in a series) refracting myriad strains of blissed synths, outernational jazz, new wave pop, post punk scuzz, screwed club and dub

Six years into Accidental Meetings’ serendipitous plot, we know to expect anything and everything from the Bristol label, so long as it's got a unique soul and does not bore. Lovely Dave ideally plays true to that brief on his 99 minute mixtape, effortlessly glyding from outernational synth folk to a killer Curtis Mayfield cover via everything from thumb piano meditations, jazz-funked sidewinders, and a proto-new beat bomb on the A-side, before swerving from gothic new wave to smudged minimal wave audities, a pitch-slapped batacuda house ace, and meter-messing skronk on the backside.

Brilliantly strange but true!
items._genre: experimental / jazz / electronic / post-punk / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张99分钟的mixtape以不断跳转的拼贴方式串联起极乐合成器、外太空合成民谣、爵士放克、拇指钢琴冥想、新节拍、哥特新浪潮、极简波、巴塔库达浩室及错拍噪音等多种声响，并穿插Curtis Mayfield翻唱。A面从世界融合民谣滑向爵士放克与原型新节拍，B面则转向暗色后朋克与扭曲节拍，整体呈现出一种难以预料的流动性。它既保留了对旋律与律动的亲和力，又在结构上刻意打破类型边界，体现了布里斯托厂牌对独特灵魂与不无聊的坚持。这张作品的价值在于其跨度本身：它不满足于单一风格的深耕，而是以混音带的形式将互不兼容的元素焊接在一起，形成一种奇异但真实的聆听体验。

items.body:
Enigmatic audity Aisie returns five years on from a strange, overlooked debut with a new suite of compressed atmospheres highly tipped FFO False Aralia, Eliza B.C., Thought Broadcast, Civilistjävel!, Hazyville-era Actress.

‘Black Fire Dream’ picks up from where 2021’s ‘Halcyon Gang Poet’ left us in a surreal, uncanny valley state of mind. The seven part, 30 minute mini-LP continues to fascinate with its cyborganic nature and dreamy otherworldliness, luring down gauzily textured, fractal wormholes where samples of “obscure educational science shows, ghost station radio transmissions, vinyl record detritus and blown-out microscopic field recordings” are gently reanimated and transmuted with a poetic sorcery. 

The whole thing feels as though it were conjuured without human touch, like the inner thoughts of an AI or machines autonomously air-syncing and executing their functions in private. With incremental stealth it breezes by in a hypnagogic haze, half-heard melodies sprouting and dissolving into the aether as granular rhythms buckle and trickle. Eyes will likely be at half mast by the end of the A-side, all the best to receive the B-side’s suggestive, illusive shadowplay of smoke and mirrors refraction and a final slope off into something like a chopped and screwed echo of Topdown Dialectic.
items._genre: experimental electronic / ambient / glitch / field recordings
items._cn_summary: 这张迷你专辑以七首曲目构成约三十分钟的声响旅程，延续了前作中 surreal 与 uncanny valley 式的氛围。素材来源包括科普节目采样、幽灵电台信号、黑胶底噪与微观田野录音，这些声音被重新拼贴与变形，形成如有机体般缓慢生长又消散的纹理。节奏颗粒细碎而不稳定，旋律片段似有若无，整体听感如同机器在无人状态下自主运作时产生的内在独白。作品在催眠般的薄雾中推进，半梦半醒之间，声音的虚实边界被反复模糊，最终滑向一种类似 chopped and screwed 处理的回声空间。这张专辑在声音设计上展现出高度的原创性与想象力，将故障感、氛围感与梦境逻辑融为一体，适合沉浸式聆听。

items.body:
Described as a "musical poem", 'Mount Analogue' is a lengthy meditation on the works of avant-garde poet and writer René Daumal that's passed from Bill Laswell and P.St (plus an ensemble featuring Nils Petter Movaer, Anna Clementi, Hideo Yamaki and others) to guitarist Henry Kaiser.

'Mount Analogue' is named after Daumel's most well-known book, the self-styled "Novel of Symbolically Authentic Non-Euclidean Adventures in Mountain Climbing" that emerged almost a decade after his early death at just 36 in 1944. That text is excerpted here on the album-length title composition, that Czech experimental sort P.ST leads on electronics alongside Laswell, Kaiser, vocalists Clementi and Percy Howard, percussionist Yamaki, cornet player Graham Haynes, violinist Dorian Cheah, Keyboardist Peter Apfelbaum and Molvaer on trumpet. It was P.St who came up with the concept in the first place and his direction helps rein in such a wide spread of contributors; from the beginning, there's a sense of calm that's rarely ruptured. Washing pebbles are augmented by instrumental washes and a deep voice reading Daumal's words in English. "Seeing that I am nothing, I desire to become. Desiring to become, I live." reads Howard over Kaiser's tangled plucks. But it's Italian-Swedish singer Clementi's part that really takes this one to the next level, bounding acrobatically over the group's wash of instrumentation to paint in brighter colors before jazzy improvisations take root.

The second disc is handled exclusively by improv legend Kaiser, who spends almost an hour pondering Alejandro Jodorowsky's 'The Holy Mountain', a film that was directly inspired by Daumal's text, on the absorbing 'Jordorowsky's Peradam', before splitting off with a set of shorter solo jams. And on the digital version, P.St turns in an album length remix of the title track that's almost as good as the original, amping up the noise and the chaos without losing hold of the track's poetic cadence.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以“音乐诗”为概念，围绕法国作家勒内·多马尔的文学作品展开，由P.ST与Bill Laswell领衔，联合众多乐手共同完成。第一碟同名长曲融合了电子声响、器乐音景、人声朗诵与爵士即兴，意大利瑞典裔歌手克莱门蒂的演唱在整体织体中跳跃穿行，带来明亮的色彩，随后转入自由的爵士即兴段落。第二碟由吉他手Henry Kaiser独立完成，受电影《圣山》启发，以近一小时的独奏延伸出深邃的冥想氛围，并附有若干短篇独奏。数字版还收录了P.ST对标题曲的全长混音，在保留原曲诗意节奏的同时增强了噪音与混沌感。整张专辑在实验、电子、爵士与即兴之间自由游走，编配开阔而从容，展现了多位艺术家在跨界合作中的默契与创造力。

items.body:
Necessary reissue of Marc Leclair’s immaculate Y2K micro-house/dub-house 12” as Akufen, dispensed by Low End Activist’s guess-again BRUK sibling to Sneaker Social Club - huge RIYL Maurizio, Studio 1, Mike Huckaby.

‘Architextures 1 -2 -3’ is a sought-after slice of hypnotic house by a noted pioneer of the micro-house movement that emerged in the late ‘90s. Its reissue arrives in the wake of a re-up for Marc Leclair’s (aka Akufen) sole solo album ‘Musique Pour 3 Femmes Enceintes’ (2005) with a strong reminder of his pivotal role in dressing house music down to fundamentals around the millennium, as deployed in Richie Hawtin mixes and praised for its exquisitely efficient, effortless, hiccuping funk.

It’s really all about the  A-side’s ‘Architexture 1’, a pendulous 127BPM roller inflected with chef’s kiss dub chords and frisky drums, on one of the smoothest, deepest basslines since ‘M5’. There’s a good reason why it’s been fetching triple figures on 2nd hand markets, so BRUK are doing the Lord’s work with this reissue, which also includes the slower, sub-heavier swivel of its Pt. 2, and more signature, strutting clip of his tight sampling tekkerz on Pt. 3.

TIP!
items._cn_summary: 这张再版发行收录了 Akufen 在千禧年前后 micro-house 运动中的代表作品，以极简的律动和精准的采样拼贴著称。A 面曲目以 127BPM 的沉稳节奏铺底，搭配 dub 风格和弦与弹性鼓组，在深邃贝斯线中构建出标志性的摇摆感。第二首降低速度、加重低频，呈现更沉缓的旋转质感；第三首则展现其紧凑的采样切分技巧。作为 micro-house 先驱，Marc Leclair 将 house 音乐剥离至基本元素，以高效而松弛的节奏逻辑影响了一批电子音乐人，作品曾被 Richie Hawtin 在混音中采用。此次由独立厂牌再版，让原本在二手市场高价流通的唱片得以重新进入公众视野。

items.body:
Dark Entries pursue prevailing interests in early ‘90s industrial club with 1st vinyl reissue of Severed Heads ’91 LP, framing Australia’s electronic dance pioneers resembling a down under New Order, early Lassigue Bendthaus or C&C in their charmingly melodic synth, EBM and techno-pop arrangements, replete with previously unheard demos and alt. mixes.

“Severed Heads reattach themselves to Dark Entries for an expanded reissue of their 1991 opus Cuisine (With Piscatorial). As originary Aussie industrial legends – although founder Tom Ellard would balk at being branded as such – Severed Heads shaped the continental subcultural sound with their kitchen electronics, chaotic tape loops, and infectious nursery-rhyme-esque melodies. Cuisine (With Piscatorial) was the long-running project’s ninth album, and is a commentary on the state of music. 

Ellard explains: “The whole food joke is really about what music’s about and how disposable it is; people have records like they have cups of coffee.” The album also presents a turn away from the dancefloor formalism of the era, which Ellard dismissed as already sufficiently explored. Cuisine brings us punchy pop kernels of the prime Heads variety, all clocking in around three minutes. Cuts like “Pilot in Hell” and “Ugly Twenties” rank among the band’s best through their deadly skewering of synth pop tropes. 

But the album also offers us a Piscatorial section, where Ellard felt free to “go fishing for ideas.” Here we get a taste of the project’s demented cut-up sensibilities, like on the “Quest for Oom Pa Pa” suite, where vintage jazz records are collaged into an angular nightmare. This double-LP reissue is the first time that Cuisine (With Piscatorial) will appear on vinyl, with a previously unreleased early version of “Seven of Oceans.” Also included is a 6-page booklet with liner notes, lyrics, and press clippings.”
items._cn_summary: Severed Heads 1991年专辑《Cuisine (With Piscatorial)》首次发行黑胶再版，收录未曝光早期版本与混音。创始人Tom Ellard以“食物”隐喻音乐工业的速朽本质，专辑既包含三分钟左右的合成器流行/EBM式短曲，以俏皮旋律解构舞曲套路，又设有“Piscatorial”段落，将爵士老唱片拼贴成扭曲的听觉梦境。整体在工业节拍、电子流行与实验剪贴之间自由游走，体现了澳大利亚电子先驱独有的怪诞感与批判性，是理解九十年代初地下电子场景多样性的重要样本。

items.body:
A leading light of neo-ambient takes their maiden bow on Glasgow’s stealthily expansive co:clear label after cherished turns with the sferic and Stroom labels.

The International Billionaire’s Love Child, or tiblsc for brevity, is the avatar of a Leipzig-based artist in possession of a distinctive, world-building ambient purview that has clearly stroked a nerve for listeners chasing the modern ambient zeitgeist, especially their couplet of ‘Delusive Tongue Shifts - Situation Based Compositions’ (2021) + ‘Hypertranslucent’ (2022). Those albums’ careful bends of pulpy sentiment and intricate, immersively dreamlike architecture is now echoed in ‘City of Something’, where her tender feel for compression and blends of HD and lo-fi tones fosters a gauzy sense of depth perception and sonorous emotional resonance. 

More so than her previous work, the eight tracks here are laced with a flickering pop spirit that riddles the album’s finely meshed dimensions, calling to mind aspects of Perila that are whisked to its most elegant frisson in ‘Resting Bitch Face’, or catching breathy contrails of an airspun pop song in ‘The Sun Really Is Something Round’, whilst tickling private parts of the imagination with the compressed artefacts of ‘You Just Want’, edging on Shinetiac’s take on smudged sheogaze trip hop in ‘Scare Me’, and teasing the most elusive urges on a secretive, quietly restive closer ‘Until the End of Time’.
items._cn_summary: TIBSLC在co:clear厂牌的首次亮相延续了她标志性的世界构建式氛围美学，将细腻的压缩感与HD、lo-fi音色交织，营造出朦胧的深度知觉与情感共振。相比前作，这八首曲目更明显地渗透着闪烁的流行精神，在精密的声响网格中融入轻柔的人声残影与空气感旋律，例如《Resting Bitch Face》中优雅的战栗感，或《The Sun Really Is Something Round》里如薄纱般飘散的流行歌曲轮廓。专辑在氛围基底上叠加了私密而躁动的细节，压缩失真与梦幻音色相互摩擦，既贴近Perila式的感性氛围，又在《Scare Me》中滑向涂抹化的shoegaze trip hop质地。整体上，它保持了实验性的声音设计，同时以更松弛的叙事节奏和隐约的流行触觉，拓展了neo-ambient的感官边界。

items.body:
Finally, Kompakt issue a true GAS outlier on vinyl for the first time, recorded in 1989 and containing some of Wolfgang Voigt’s earliest and starkest recycling of magisterial Wagner loops, closest to the ends of The Caretaker, Philip Jeck, Kevin Drumm.

One of those releases that has lurked on our shelves since 2008 as a book and CD, ‘November 89’ exists in the margins of Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS canon as its creepiest and most occluded evocation of long walks in the Bavarian forests. While other GAS classics ooze a sort of dappled warmth breaking thru the trees in their widescreen dub techno strolls, you can fully feel the light dying over the horizon and the forest drawing in on this particularly gloomy, hour-long suite. 

As the title suggests, it was mostly, remarkably, made in ’89, back when Voigt was finding his feet between techno, house and indie-pop, and nearly a decade before he co-founded Kompakt with Michael Mayer & Jürgen Paape - by which time he was a full-fledged rave dynamo as Love Inc. and myriad others notable projects. And, in that sense, it can be heard as his ‘Selected Ambient Works 89-95’ - or perhaps more pertinently with SAW II vibes - in his nascent attempt to chase the ambient dragon, which surely endures for its strangely nostalgic, unheimlich qualities.

An educated guess leads us to think the first three were made in ’89, taking in the nightfall scenery of smudged symphonic strings and icy crackle to ‘Der Wald’, plus the muddied bass waltz and spectral pall of ‘Das Moor’, thru the self-evidently titled centrepiece ‘1989-11-01’, bristling with a digitally iridescent dread. ‘Tal 90’ and ‘Nah Und Fern’, which shares its title with the 2008 boxset, were most likely made a little later, and find the wintry doom thawing to the GAS-eous forms we’ve all come to deeply know and adore. 

A true evergreen for deep ambient techno connoisseurs, no less
items._genre: ambient / dark ambient / dub techno / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张作品是沃尔夫冈·福格特在GAS项目中的异类，录制于一九八九年，后以书与CD形式流传，此次由科隆厂牌首次发行黑胶。它不像GAS经典那样以宽银幕科技舞曲透出林间暖光，而是用瓦格纳乐句的循环、模糊弦乐与冰冷底噪构成一小时长的阴郁组曲，令人感到光线在森林边缘消失。早期段落带有数字光泽的恐惧感，后半部分则逐渐解冻为更接近后世GAS的形态。评论将其与凯尔·提克特、菲利普·耶克和凯文·德拉姆的暗色声响相提并论，是深暗环境科技舞曲脉络中的独特样本。

items.body:
St Circul's debut album "Ley Lines" via Archaic Vaults.

"Concise collection of folkloric grime instrumentals to rise from a new moniker taken on by the elusive First Circle. A breadcrumb trail of effortlessly crafted early 2000s-era grime, trap and drill instrumentals can be found on a fairly sparse Soundcloud account and numerous NTS shows spanning the last ten years, on which he is known to play almost entirely his own material. Now a different energy takes hold on »Ley Lines«: ten tracks by the enigmatic producer to be released both on a label and in physical format for the first time.

»Ley Lines« was born from a meandering quest through South London’s more leafy dwellings. These cherished regions became a place of refuge in which to ruminate on the hopes that love and community can outlast the dwindling state of Britain’s social and political climate. Photo documentation was made which would later form the genesis for each track, and a return to the studio resulted in something which could not be fitted into the existing First Circle discography.

Harpsichord and brass samples (»A Plan Is Formed«, »Hilly Fields«) are underpinned by murky bass loops and tight militaristic percussion – motifs recognisable amongst white label grime’s most influential producers (Wiley, Skepta, Lewi White etc.) that push the formula into far more rapturous territories than any of FC’s previous productions. The more introspective moments of the album (»Wares at the Ivy House«, »Blythe Vision«) put local field recordings and devotional reverberant ambience to the forefront, alluding to St Circul’s proto-dungeon synth influences and giving the whole album a unique world all its own.

Archaic Vaults is proud to host an album which shares intrinsic roots with the label’s own South London birthplace. »Ley Lines«’ ten tracks of psychogeographic drifting are available in digital and limited cassette format via Archaic Vaults.

Mastered by Owen Pratt Design by Severin Black Artwork image by St Circul"
items._genre: grime / experimental / electronic / ambient / field recording
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是St Circul（First Circle的新化名）的首张正式专辑，以十首器乐作品呈现。制作灵感源于南伦敦绿地区域的漫步，照片记录成为每首曲目的起点。声响上，古键琴与铜管采样被置于浑浊贝斯和严谨军事化打击乐之下，延续早期grime、trap与drill的脉络，同时将当地田野录音与带有回响的虔诚氛围推到前台，隐约透出前地牢合成器的影响。整体在粗粝的舞曲肌理中融入心理地理式的漫游感，并试图以社区与爱回应英国社会政治气候的萎靡。专辑由独立厂牌Archaic Vaults发行，首次以实体磁带形式呈现。

items.body:
All killer, no filler trotters from a golden period of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry’s foundational work at fabled studio, The Black Ark.

This 3rd in a prized series spies the wee madman conjuring multidimensional spectres from vocal recordings of regular spars: Max Romeo, The Jolly Brothers, Leroy Sibbles, The Mistic, and Devon Irons. Perry’s visionary, innovative application of studio-as-instrument tekkerz come to the fore in the music’s layered diffusions, which we may take for granted in contemporary music, but was radical back then, and whose uncanny appeal has only steeped with age. 

Including a solo standout in the ghostly, harmonised roots wooze of his ‘Dread Lion’ gem as King Scratch, it spans the signature, lysergic sparkle of his ‘Conscious Man’cut with The Jolly Brothers, thru a stepping 12” mix of Max Romeo’s ‘Norman’ (1978), and heat-hazed sway to Leroy Sibbles’ ‘Garden of Life’, along with The Mistic’s eyes-down devotional ‘Forward With Jah’, and sloshing nyabingi of ‘When Jah Comes’ for Devon Irons.
items._genre: dub / reggae / roots reggae / experimental / psychedelic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Lee Perry在Black Ark录音室黄金时期的五首混音作品，合作者包括Max Romeo、The Jolly Brothers、Leroy Sibbles等。Perry将录音室本身作为乐器，通过层叠的混响、延迟与相位处理，把原始人声录音转化为多维的声响空间，呈现出当时极为激进的制作理念。曲目涵盖Dread Lion中幽灵般的和声与根源律动、Conscious Man的迷幻光泽、Norman的步进节拍，以及Garden of Life的湿热摇摆，整体在dub的厚重低音与roots reggae的灵性脉络中，融入大量实验性声场扩散与迷幻元素。这些手法在当代音乐中已被广泛沿用，但在七十年代末的牙买加语境下显得格外超前，且随着时间推移愈发彰显其独特魅力。

items.body:
Jake Muir returns to enmossed with an album of "all goop’d up ambient bits from black and death metal records...", stirring together an atmospheric, bathhouse-ready reaction to the most extreme soundscapes, enhancing lysergic moments to bring out parallels with gear from Coil, :zoviet*france:, Pinkcourtesyphone, Main or even Ulver.

What makes music heavy, exactly? Is it simply the volume itself, or could it be the spread of culturally assured elements that make our skin prickle and our ears focus in on fight or flight terrors like animalistic cries, rattling chains or grim liturgical chants? Muir has been fascinated with Rock music since he was a kid, poring over byzantine, maximal offerings from bands like Meshuggah and Nine Inch Nails. And it's an obsession that's led him through the bullrushes of death and black metal, genres that often veer into experimental territory, crossing streams with industrial, noise and, of course, dark ambient. 'Pareidolia' is Muir's celebration of metal's nightmarish atmospheres, sounds that make the blast beats, hoarse vocals and smudgy chords sound even more substantial without technically being loud. 

Pulled away from their context, these textures are compellingly theatrical: whooshing ice winds, creaking branches, scraping metal, chiming bells, plucked strings and heaving drones. They're sounds that situate us in the scene’s ancestral Northern homeland, in some remote cabin hemmed in by harsh weather and prowling wolves. Heard on their own, it's predictable that we end up trudging similarly cinematic territory as the "dark ambient" forebears like Lustmord and Deathprod or more recent exponents Svarte Greiner and Lussuria. Muir's idea for the album was a little different; spurred on by his back-and-forth with Even Caminiti on 2022's ace 'Talisman' album, he attempted to use these bleak fantasies to power the kind of heady, sexually-charged moods that goosebump'd thru his breakout 'Bathhouse Blues' without losing the folk horror cogitation of last year's sacred meditation 'Campana Sonans'.

In fact, 'Pareidolia' is supposed to play like an illusion - even the name of the album is a reference to these phantom arrangements. Muir wants to rope us in with familiarity before waltzing us through a parallel history of isolationist, industrial ambient gear, the kind of guitar-muddling, metal-aware grot that linked Nocturnal Emissions and Z'EV and Robert Hampson's electroacoustic rock duo Main with heady set texts from Eno, Daniel Lanois, Stuart Dempster and Steve Roach. The album isn't just a collage of the quiet moments from recent RYM metal side-quests, as you'll hear as soon as you plug into opener 'Beithir'. Between the blustery soundscapes and knife-sharpening SFX, there's a melodic pulse and echoing oscillations that wouldn't sound out of place on an IASOS record, while the dense, Sunn O)))-adjacent bass drone takes on a surprisingly humid character, winding itself around weightless pads and spirit breaths.

It's the air that's heavy, not the music itself.
items._cn_summary: Jake Muir 在《Pareidolia》中从黑金属与死亡金属的极端声响里提取氛围碎片，将嘶吼、爆裂鼓点与刺耳和弦剥离原语境，转化为由冰风、树枝断裂、金属刮擦、钟鸣和沉重嗡鸣构成的听觉剧场。专辑以“幻想性错觉”为概念，试图用这些幽暗素材营造兼具情欲张力与民间恐怖沉思的沉浸体验，延续了与 Even Caminiti 合作《Talisman》时的互动思路，也呼应了 Bathhouse Blues 的潮湿氛围感。Muir 将金属的沉重感重新定义为文化暗示而非音量本身，使作品在 Lustmord、Deathprod 等黑暗氛围传统之外，融入 Nocturnal Emissions、Z'EV、Main 等工业与电声音乐脉络，形成一种既熟悉又错位的平行历史叙事。开篇曲 Beithir 在风声与磨刀音效间浮现旋律脉冲，厚重低音嗡鸣带有 Sunn O)))-式质感，却因轻盈音垫与呼吸感而呈现意外的湿润气质，展现了对极端声响进行氛围化重构的独特手法。

items.body:
Japan’s Joe Fujinoki makes a sort of dungeon variant of dub techno, sounding something like the far fringes of the Chain Reaction label if it were excavated and screwed by Aaron Dilloway. Trust it’s completely off the rails, pulsing with life and landing somewhere between Vainqueur, Tolerance, AOKI takamasa, Rashad Becker, Pole.

There's clearly enough life left in the motions and aesthetics of Dub Techno (and its "ambient" progeny) that every so often, someone digs out the defibrillator and shocks it back to life. This time, the paddles are handled by Tokyo-based operative Joe Fujinoki, who retains dub's latent eccentricity - the kinda unsteady, obstreperous genius that runs thru everything from Lee Perry to Basic Channel - while steering the chaos into murky new territory. Inspired by "the fragility of the human body", Fujinoki extends the potential of his arsenal of analog instruments by mimicking the fluid movements of the natural world, creating a circulatory system of all-electronic sequences that feels peculiarly animate, its rhythms falling in-and-out of time like heartbeats and its tones dipping and winding like snatched breaths. 

Rather than sculpting his stack of oscillators into a familiarly fluttering nostalgia trigger, Fujinoki zeroes in on their most unstable tendencies, following a path laid out by Stefan Betke on those stone-cold-classic early Pole records, glitch milestones that emerged from the ashes of his broken Waldorf 4-Pole filter, and of course Vladislav Delay’s curving of uneven basslines and rickety clicks and pops through his loose lattice of echoes. Just peep 'Sculptural Dub I' and you'll see know what we're on about, shaping its low end into wormy spirals that inch around ping-ponging metallic smacks that wouldn't sound out of place on one of Torsten Pröfrock's most enigmatic libations.

'Limb' starts off as if it's gonna launch into a Basic Channel tribute, with distant, aching pads and a 'Lyot Rmx'-style echoed stab and quickly oozes towards total abstraction, pegging its harmonic elements to scratchy rhythmic clusters and gruff interferences. At times, 'Glass Torso' plays more like a DIY noise record, the kind of off-piste synth vs tape experiment you'd expect to find on iDEAL, or rediscovered for a timeline-distorting anthology reissue, like that stone-cold-killer Tolerance box set from a few years back. Check 'Hollow', with its blood-curdling dissonance and ghoulish pseudo-generative gurgles, or the waterlogged, freewheeling rhythms that anchor the album's euphoric closing track 'Still' and tell us it ain't special. You know what to do!
items._genre: dub techno / experimental / glitch / dark ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将dub techno推向暗黑而失控的边界，以模拟合成器与磁带实验模拟人体与自然界的流动状态，节奏如心跳般忽快忽慢，音色如呼吸般扭曲蜿蜒。受早期Pole的故障美学与Vladislav Delay松散回声网络影响，作品在极简律动中植入刺耳干扰、血腥不和谐音与伪生成式咕噜声，既有Basic Channel式回响残影，又滑向DIY噪音与即兴磁带拼贴的领域。整体呈现出一种非机械的、近乎有机的律动感，在幽闭空间感与抽象声响之间取得平衡，尤其适合追求实验性与氛围张力的听众。

items.body:
First time reissue of Wolfgang Voigt's foundational first GAS album since its release in 1996 - it remains the archetype for so much contemporary ambient music and back-room techno, melting camouflaged German cultural references into a timeless, anthemic pulse. This new reissue is the original extended vinyl version, with definitive longer versions of the six classic tracks. Available in deluxe 3LP and single CD editions.

By the mid-'90s, techno had become the language of German youth culture, tied up in the country's long history of electronic musical innovation - from Kluster to Kraftwerk - and the revolutionary cry of reunification when the Berlin Wall fell in 1989. Based in Köln, Voigt had already put his stamp on dance music by the time he embarked on the mysterious GAS project, working alongside his brother Reinhard to help devise the sound that would evolve into minimal techno, but GAS felt different - more illusory, hypnotic. 

The name, aside from accurately describing the vaporous ambience that whispers through each track, stands for Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and it was Voigt's concept to not only express the feeling of dropping acid in the Königsforst, a verdant woodland only a short drive from Köln, but to distill centuries of German music into a contemporary haze that reflected a hopeful new era. And after testing the waters with '95's Profan-released EP 'Modern', Voigt set a new benchmark with 'GAS', laying out his narrative over six long movements, the shortest of which clocks in at just under 12 minutes.

Voigt wasn't interested in making songs, exactly, but emphasizing texture, burying samples of traditional German music - from baroque to schlager - in murky drones punctuated by squashed 4/4 rhythms. Not dance music exactly, it's headphone gear that's referencing the dance canon in its shift from the US, through Jamaica and the UK to Germany. Much like the Artificial Intelligence era in the UK, it imprints the familiar cycles (pulsing kick drums, undulating soundsystem-ready basslines) with its own regional character. It's no mistake that Voigt begins with an entirely beatless composition that paints the landscape without revealing the complete palette. The album's airiest track, 'GAS 1' is a stylistic milestone - something we can hear tracking thru electronic music from then until now; just listen to Jan Jelinek, Vladislav Delay, PAN's 'Mono No Aware' comp, or anything on the West Mineral imprint. It's ambient music, but where Eno's vision was trained on an earlier era, Voigt had cut his teeth on acid house, hardcore and Detroit techno, and was able to muddle those influences with his own homegrown obsessions. 

That famous, omnipresent filtered kick makes its first appearance on 'GAS 2', thudding beneath watery glitches and sweeping orchestral pads. Voigt doesn't make his concept too vivid (at least at this stage in its evolution), but the outline of classical music is there, punctured by mesmerising minimal thuds that as yet hadn't become a meme. It's not music that develops, it exists, freezing a moment in time and letting the mind pick out a scene, concentrating on the organic, shifting harmonies rather than the static beat. If acid house was all about the squelch, this was all about vapour, as sample-rich pads seem to disappear into clouds of static, blooming from the density. There's a more evident schlager-inspired swing on 'GAS 4' that Voigt and his Kompakt crew would explore more in the coming years, but it's contorted into a subterranean rumble, and on 'GAS 5', the producer tentatively glances trance's quivering euphoria, using reverb and delay to turn anthemic stabs into whooshing melodic rushes. 

If you haven't managed to hear GAS before, this is the perfect starting point, and if you've only heard the album in its truncated form (both the CD release and the 'Nah und Fern' version were incomplete), then we've got to say this is the one.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Wolfgang Voigt于1996年以GAS之名发表的首张作品，此次再版还原了原始加长版六首曲目。它并非传统舞曲，而是将德国巴洛克至流行小调的传统音乐采样埋入浑浊的持续音与压缩的4/4节拍中，营造出迷幻、催眠般的氛围。专辑以一首完全无拍子的作品开场，逐步展开其声音景观，标志性的滤波底鼓在第二曲中浮现。乐评认为它奠定了当代氛围音乐与后场techno的原型，将德国文化记忆与电子舞曲语言融合，既呼应了90年代中期德国青年文化与统一后的时代情绪，也影响了后来的Jan Jelinek、Vladislav Delay等众多电子音乐人。作品强调纹理而非旋律，适合耳机聆听，在氛围音乐与techno之间建立了独特的地域性声音叙事。

items.album: H. Flora ~ bioacoustic recordings from Thailand / Noumenon
items.excerpt: Over the course of a month-long bicycle journey across southern and central Thailand, H. Flora accumulated a personal archive of nocturnal field recordings. These recordings became the basis for two interconnected releases, each approaching the same ecosystems from a different perspective. Anthropause presents the material in its raw form: rainforests alive with gibbons, amphibian choirs, Tokay geckos, bats and insects captured during the hours when human activity had receded to its minimum.
