items.body: “Berani” means “the exile”, and it follows someone who leaves home in search of freedom and a better future. Rabie Houti made that move himself, leaving Oran, the Algerian city where raï took shape, for Montpellier around 2014. “Berani” is the second single from his upcoming album, after “Rwahou“. A violinist and singer, Houti leads the Rabie Houti Band, drawn from Montpellier’s cross-cultural music scene. His Algerian violin, rooted in the Arab-Andalusian repertoire, leads a band that pitches it against electric blues guitar, drums, bass and synths. The EP that “Berani” trails leans harder into rock than his earlier records. He belongs to the sono mondiale lineage, the French world-music movement whose defining figure was Rachid Taha, the Algerian-French singer who drove raï and chaabi into rock. Stream “Berani” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Rabie Houti – Berani appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: 《流亡》意为“放逐”，讲述离乡者追寻自由与更好生活的旅程，也对应拉比·胡提本人从阿尔及利亚奥兰移居法国蒙彼利埃的经历。作为新专辑第二支单曲，作品以根植于阿拉伯-安达卢西亚传统的阿尔及利亚小提琴为核心，与电声布鲁斯吉他、鼓、贝斯和合成器形成对撞；相比早期作品，这张唱片更偏向摇滚。胡提所属的法国世界音乐运动可追溯至拉希德·塔哈，后者曾将北非拉伊与沙比音乐推进摇滚语境。值得关注的是，传统弦乐在当代电声编制中并未被淹没，而是以清晰的旋律线条与电吉他、合成器音色彼此撕扯；流散身份也由此转化为声音上的冲突与融合。

items.body: It's rare to come back home empty-handed from a foray into Corbett vs Dempsey’s territorial waters, and this mission is no exception. Today, we're talking about the Atlantic Pact, set between the ever-erupting, volcanic Chicago scene and the anarcho-free stronghold of Amsterdam, that nothing and no one will ever conquer. No drones, tanks, Patriots, or F-35s, but the only weapons useful to humanity: reeds, pianos, drums, and basses. These Things Happen provide them with their sophomore album, "A Gentle Reminder", following their 2022 self-titled debut. This album, recorded at Hyde Park Jazz Festival in Chicago and at WNUR Studio, Northwestern University, confirms the band's recipe: original songs interspersed with renditions of Misha Mengelberg and Thelonious Monk, presented not in a slavish, calligraphic manner but through a contemporary reinterpretation of tradition. The players on the field deserve to be met up close. Keefe Jackson, tenor saxophone, bass clarinet. Born in Fayetteville, Arkansas, he arrived in Chicago in 2001 and performed across US and Europe with the likes of Tomeka Reid, Tim Days, Dave Rempis, Mike Reed, Jeb Bishop, Jason Adasiewicz, Satoko Fujii, Ab Baars and Bill Meyer. His partner in crime on the other side of the Pond, Oscar Jan Hoogland, piano, is a top notch badass. A leading figure on the Dutch impro scene, Hoogland sprung onto the Amsterdam landscape around 20 years ago, at the forefront of a new group of improvisers to arrive and simultaneously uphold the tradition of New Dutch Swing even while tearing it apart. As always, collaborations define the breadth of a musician's chromatic palette and so, read here about Oscar: improvisation with Senegalese singer Mola Sylla and percussionist Frank Rosaly; sound installations and performances with Practical Music and his Phonograph Orchestra; cumbia with Ibelisse Guardia Ferraguttis’s Superinca and the Galactic Green; Ethiopian jazz and Eritrean traditional music with Semer Welday’s Adulis. His work with Arnold de Boer and the duo with mythologic Han Bennink incontrovertibly attests to the caliber of the artist. The rhythm section that supports the two pals features Jason Roebke on double bass (collaborations with Ken Vandermark, Jeb Bishop, Jeff Parker, Chad Taylor, and Rob Mazurek), who replaced Joshua Abrams during the process, and Mikel Patrick Avery on drums (Rob Mazurek, Marshall Allen Tomeka Reid, Jeff Parker, and Kurt Vile on his CV). The record: Jackson's opening track "20 Years Past 12 O'Clock," a sonic excursus that moves across multiple time scales, is followed by a piece by Hoogland dedicated to Ab Baars, "Upperclass Underground," and a reinterpretation of Monk’s "Green Chimneys," whose genesis is described as follows: "it started out as a punk song on the setlist before taking a thin-threaded turn on the night." Two original compositions keep the pace in the right mood, constantly balancing compositional rigor with a loose flow, free from excessive constraints. The revisitation of Mengelberg's "Een Beetje Zenuwachtig," from minor to major, pays homage to the legendary Ukrainian pianist's key change when he played "Round Midnight" in Chicago, while "Well You Needn't" pushes Monk "max so far," as Hoogland puts it, with a sculptural declination of an ongoing sonic pendulum swinging between modernity and tradition. The album closes with “Over het Zijn en het Hoera”, its title drawn from an absurdist story by Dutch writer and artist Armando. As it has rightly been said, this is music that knows its history inside out and wears it lightly. The generosity of spirit here, between players, between cities, between Monk and Mengelberg, between composition and the moment, is the real subject. You know, sometimes things like these happen. A Gentle Reminder by These Things Happen Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是芝加哥与阿姆斯特丹两大即兴场景的跨洋对话，由萨克斯手Keefe Jackson与钢琴手Oscar Jan Hoogland领衔，搭配低音提琴手Jason Roebke与鼓手Mikel Patrick Avery。录音分别取自芝加哥海德公园爵士音乐节和西北大学WNUR电台，延续了乐队首张专辑的路线：原创曲目与对Misha Mengelberg、Thelonious Monk作品的当代重释交替出现，并非照搬原曲的旋律框架，而是以即兴思维重新拆解传统素材。开篇曲跨越多种时间尺度，Hoogland献给Ab Baars的曲目以及Monk的《Green Chimneys》都体现出作曲严谨性与松散流动感的平衡。两位主奏者分别扎根于芝加哥自由爵士和荷兰新即兴场景，合作中既有火山般的爆发力，也有细致的声音对话，节奏组的替换与磨合进一步塑造了专辑的现场感与室内乐质感。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以贝斯为绝对主角，在爵士、摇滚与前卫融合的框架中展开高密度演奏。多位客座乐手参与，包括与Willow Smith合作的摇滚曲目以及邀请Dennis Chambers助阵的放克曲目，各声部均展现高度技术性。作为来自印度的音乐人，Mohini Dey在西方融合语境中注入个人身份，贝斯线条始终处于最前台，音色与律动兼具冲击力。专辑适合追求演奏技巧与融合编曲的听众。

items.body: Water will always follow the path of least resistance, trickling along and naturally finding the easiest course. It does so effortlessly, without thought. Of course, life is rarely like that…but somehow, things usually have a way of working out for the best. Relationships may turn to ash and dreams may be broken, but life has a way of (eventually) settling down. Glorious things await, and they wouldn’t have been possible without heartache or pain. Even at the lowest ebb, there is always hope, and accelerated growth is possible after experiencing pain. From ground level, what looks messy and blinded by fog can look crystal clear from a bird’s-eye view. Battle-worn, the heart can recover and be all the stronger for its experience. The pandemic has been a ripe blossom for creativity, even at a time when the rest of the world experienced stagnation, confinement, and death. In 2020, music, creativity, and the arts in general all grew with the advent of lockdowns and the absence of light. Matt Robertson’s ‘Enveleau’ (Subtempo, April 30) finds envelopment, peace, and ultimately gratitude in and among its surroundings, be it in the solitude of lockdown or out in the open. No matter where you are, you can be thankful for where you’ve been planted. Robertson’s ambient sound and subtle, flexible electronics combine with organic techno to produce radiant and effervescent music. It’s benefitted from being in and enjoying its own surroundings; you get the feeling that Robertson loved every minute of creation and recording, pouring it all into every tweak and tonal transmutation. Rhythms are crisp, lean, and in great shape, but there are also jaw-dropping ambient vistas to gaze upon, such as the sublime ‘Syntropic’, which features glowing sunset synths and a glorious, expanding atmosphere. The music doesn’t have to work hard to make things happen; it naturally follows the path of least resistance. It should be like that with the right person, too. You won’t have to work so hard to be happy when you find them. It will just happen. Like Enveleau, life is smoother when you go with the flow. www.subtempo.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以环境声响与有机电子节拍为核心，在沉静与律动之间取得平衡。乐评强调其音乐如同水流般自然展开，不刻意制造冲突，而是通过细腻的合成器音色与灵活的电子纹理营造出通透、明亮的氛围。作品在隔离时期创作，却并未流露压抑，反而带有一种从困境中生长出的宁静与感恩。其中《Syntropic》被特别提及，以落日般的合成器光辉和不断扩展的空间感构成令人沉浸的声景。节奏部分精炼而富有弹性，整体听感流畅且具有呼吸感，适合在独处或开放环境中聆听。专辑由Subtempo发行，展现了创作者在声音细节上的投入，每一处音色变化都显得从容而富有生命力。

items.body: Lifelines is an aptly-named series from Slowcraft Records. In this year of all years, music, love, and friendship is vital. They are lifelines to millions. When the world is drowning in grief and suffering, these things are rafts to hold onto. Sometimes, the only thing to do is to hold on for dear life, knowing that, for however long it may take, better days are ahead. The pairing of Dominik Grenzler and Stijn Hüwels on Where We Meet has ushered in a record that is sorely needed: one of ‘friendship, hope, and steadfast, creative spirit’. The digital-only series, curated by Slowcraft founder James Murray, presents consoling works from high-calibre artists; musicians who don’t fit a typical mould, but choose to break down and split from genre conventions and expectations to produce something adventurous and innovative. Mastering duties have gone to the ever-excellent Ian Hawgood, while beautiful artwork from printmaker June Murray is also featured. Recorded between Zurich and Leuven during 2020’s Spring lockdown, Where We Meet is the first collaboration between Grenzler and Hüwels. It’s an essential record, not only down to its timing and window of release, but in its mood, attitude, and approach, as the music offers an outlet and a getaway from the ills of 2020 and its deluge of trouble and stress. A wet reverb and an elongated drone open up the album, stretching and joining up with a piano’s soft, twinkling notes and introducing an array of quiet, micro-tonal sounds in the background. Those sounds are unobtrusive, entering at random intervals and gracing the background with their presence. The reverb is more like a light spray than an anchor, but it’s a constant, comforting presence, and one that can influence and colour every aspect of the music, making it shimmer and ripple. Where We Meet is music that could melt at any temperature. The music is given space to develop, maximising the fruits of this collaboration and turning potential into realization. The drones are subtle in their movements, and a piano occasionally enters with some light, dispersed playing. Electronic sounds scuttle and swim, leaving a deep reverb in their wake. Many are in need of a lifeline today. Where We Meet will pull you to safety. www.slowcraft.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominik Grenzler与Stijn Hüwels在2020年春季封锁期间首次合作的成果，由Slowcraft Records以数字形式发行。音乐以湿润的混响和延绵的长音铺陈，钢琴轻柔闪烁的音符穿插其间，背景中散布着细微的微音调声响，电子声音如游动般浮现又留下深沉余韵。作品给予声音充分的生长空间，让两位艺术家的对话从潜在可能转化为实际呈现。整张专辑在氛围与电子之间游走，既保持环境音乐的沉静特质，又通过细腻的声音层次和空间处理展现实验性。其创作意图并非单纯提供听觉背景，而是以声音构建一种可以依偎的庇护所，回应2020年弥漫的焦虑与隔绝感，成为听者情感上的救生索。专辑由Ian Hawgood负责母带，June Murray提供版画封面，整体呈现独立厂牌特有的手工艺质感与人文温度。

items.body: Saariselka’s debut album ‘The Ground Our Sky’ looks out at a wide horizon and up at the stars, offering a new brand of cosmic, ambient Americana. Saariselka, a team-up between composer Marielle Jakobsons (Fender Rhodes, organ, synthesizers) and Chuck Johnson (pedal steel guitar, electronic treatments), paint a gorgeous landscape of instrumental introspection and contemplation; it brims with light and life. The Ground Our Sky is inspired by the meeting of earth and light. An old Norse myth says that the great northern glaciers stored energy until they burst with fluorescent light, creating the Aurora Borealis, and Saariselka’s music contains a similar outpouring of light, a radiant, glowing energy bearing fruit of a positive, soothing nature while keeping its eyes on the infinite. Music is a life force, and their music is alive with reverberating Americana and lilting lap-steel. Streaks of light surround the listener, and vocals dissect the air, delivering elemental song. Standing on earth (the ground) while casting an upwards glance into the cosmos (our sky), Saariselka deliver a spectacular album of high originality and stunning musicianship, blending science with dream, dream with philosophy, and philosophy with human understanding. Sparse electric guitar notes ring into the atmosphere, becoming a part of space, linking and individually lighting up to reveal a melodic constellation. A disembodied voice is cradled in the melody, while the atmosphere slinks and sinks into its surroundings, hovering over the tips of mountains and gracing the cusp of its peaks; a touchpoint between the earth and the air. The music is a meeting-point, too, a doorway connecting the two worlds, shifting between the grounded realism of the physical plane (and the restrictions posed by gravity), and the limitless potential of discovery which waits in the higher altitudes, even past the troposphere and into the black gulfs of space. Jakobsons co-founded Date Palms, so the startlingly original music on The Ground Our Sky shouldn’t come as a surprise. Mixing instrumental finesse with yummy dream-pop (and splashing it in the arid, windswept hues of Americana), the music is somehow able to reach the stars even while the shoes remain glued to the earth. The Ground Our Sky by Saariselka www.saariselka.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由作曲家Marielle Jakobsons与Chuck Johnson合作，以Fender Rhodes、风琴、合成器与踏板钢棒吉他构建出兼具宇宙视野与大地质感的氛围美式音乐。作品灵感源于北欧神话中冰川积蓄能量爆发为极光的意象，音乐中充满流动的光感与舒缓的生机。稀疏的电吉他音符在空间中扩散，人声被旋律轻柔包裹，整体氛围仿佛悬浮于山巅，连接着地表与苍穹。专辑将器乐细节、梦幻流行色彩与美式荒原的干涸色调交织在一起，在脚踩大地与仰望星空之间形成独特的听觉通道，展现出鲜明的原创性与跨风格融合能力。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 专辑以乌克兰传统歌曲和原创作品为素材，围绕俄罗斯从乌克兰东部绑架约两万名儿童的战争罪行展开。演唱由Marichka与Alina Kuzma共同主导，加拿大和乌克兰两地女性乐手参与，编制以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉、钢琴和双陶笛。乐评人刻意先不阅读歌词，仅凭音乐判断其声乐与器乐表现已足够有力；随后阅读翻译时被歌词打动。《Foreign Land》改编自传统歌谣，原述少女被送往异乡帮佣，亦对应今日被掳儿童的处境，Marichka的演唱温柔克制。《Rusalka》则由Alina Kuzma领唱，转向激烈粗粝，呼应神话传说中的自然精灵。专辑在传统民歌基底上融入当代议题，以女性集体声音传递哀痛与抵抗。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦圣多美和普林西比在非洲黄金年代录制的Puxa音乐，延续第一辑的感染力。Puxa融合了前葡萄牙非洲殖民地的多种节奏，并吸收merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等元素，形成复杂而热烈的舞曲风格。专辑中多把吉他相互交织缠绕，主唱与和声不断应答，成为旋律框架的一部分；节奏组在部分曲目中刻意留白，让鼓与吉他驱动律动。乐评还提到Puxa舞蹈曾遭葡萄牙殖民者禁止，但音乐依然延续至今。合辑由独立厂牌Bongo Joe发行，收录Pedro Lima、Sangazuza、Africa Negra等艺人的15首作品，展现了这些人口稀少的岛屿上丰富的音乐生态与独特文化视角。

items.excerpt:

The Gods Laugh

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了贝宁传奇乐队Poly-Rythmo与歌手Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的作品。Dougbé被称为“魔鬼总理”，既是伏都教实践者，也是节奏的召唤者，他通过拍打腿部演绎源自刚果的Cavacha律动，并与乐队合作留下短暂而强烈的录音。音乐根植于70年代放克，但录音质感和合成器音色已带有80年代特征；古巴son的影响在开篇曲目中尤为明显，而刚果伦巴则贯穿始终。典型曲目如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，闪烁的吉他与密集踩镲构建出持续张力；《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则呈现更直白的古巴风格，牛铃、鼻音呼应与紧凑重复的段落交织。整张合辑展示了贝宁地域文化、伏都信仰与跨大西洋节奏传统的融合，是理解西非放克与伦巴交汇的重要资料。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威音乐家合作，将主要来自两国的传统舞曲重新诠释为一种室内乐式的对话。三位乐手分别以提琴、竖笛和鼓/打击乐展开亲密而细致的互动，并不为舞者服务，而是深入旋律背后隐藏的可能性，呈现出斯堪的纳维亚民间音乐中沉郁、神秘甚至不安的一面。开篇选曲源自挪威塞特斯达尔谷地，水妖传说为音乐增添了一层关于琴魔与禁忌的暗色。演奏中，领奏旋律与即兴纹理交织，某些段落甚至从行进中突然碎裂、停顿，显示他们有意打破传统舞曲的规整结构。值得聆听的是，这种处理并非将民谣简单电声化或爵士化，而是在保留原曲骨架的同时，用室内乐般的敏感和实验性的叙事感，让传统曲调显露出更丰富的心理维度。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / experimental / hip hop
items._cn_summary: 这是一份来自芝加哥枪击幸存者的街头录音档案，由制作人Ian Brennan在社区门廊前录制，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。录音中没有添加任何音乐，仅保留环境声与即兴说唱，呈现了枪击暴力阴影下普通人的真实声音。一位失去两个儿子的老人哽咽道歉，一位刚从追悼会赶来的妇女，以及飞机起降噪音、蚊虫和街上的野狗，共同构成了这张专辑的底色。它更像是一份社会现场的声音文献，而非传统意义上的音乐作品，其力量来自不加修饰的真实与沉默背后的结构性不平等。该项目收益捐赠给Cure Violence Global，以支持以健康方式终结暴力的行动。

items.body: Review by arymenezes — Progarchives is my primary source of information, and this album was one of the excellent discoveries I made here.It begins with incredible keyboard phrasing. The drums add many inventive layers to the harmonies. At the minute-and-a-half mark, there are some passages reminiscent of ELP, featuring combinations of different keyboards. They manage to keep the energy high-voltage throughout its entire length.The piano on the second track is vibrant, and the drum rhythms create a smoothy contemplative swing feel. Overall, the result is reminiscent of cabaret music mixed with blues-rock. It is a very short track featuring vocals, whereas the preceding track is instrumental.Their compositional skills are truly highlighted on this music, as they seek out very organic and fluid harmonies. The arrangements are also quite interesting, as the role of the bass is more clearly defined, this time, through the keyboards and bass drums. The drum turnovers always reveal new subtleties when executed.Another track featuring vocals, which are always in english. For now, the style leans more towards rock, with a pronounced drum beat. Instead of traditional guitar solos, the solo sections are performed on the only two instruments used.The blues returns on the 5th track, taking on a slightly danceable feel. It isn't a masterpiece of creativity or diversity, but it certainly gets the job done.The sixth track sticks with some beautiful blues but employs arrangements and tones quite different from those used previously. They excel at knowing how to highlight the most inspired instrument ? in this case, the keyboards ? through the mix and editing. Even the drum fills have a bluesy atmosphere. It's a short track.The organ opening of the next track is enchanting, increasing the atmosphere with a more spiritual quality. After nearly a minute and a half of this, the rest of the instruments and the vocals enter respectfully. The unhurried tempo maintains a sense of reverence and transcendence. The composition concludes with the organ ? an emotive finish that layers sounds with clarity and consistency. It is no coincidence that this is the album's longest track, 'cause it's one of the most inspired.The vocals are (effectively) sustained on the eighth track. The cadence remains on the slower side. In a way, it is like hearing a second take on the musical concept explored in the previous track. The organ's timbre is truly wonderful.The next track is a magnificent adaptation of Ravel's 'Bolero' with a kraut flavor. It is intense, like the original composition, with the added advantage of being a condensed version.A more melodic approach prevails on the 10th track. Once again, the pairing of piano and organ creates a fabulous, ethereal combination. It is a shame the sound is a bit muffled.The final track on the LP is pure Krautrock. Electronic harmonies blend together with great freedom. The drums are situated that feel halfway between a march and a loop; to my ears, a great tune.My edition of the CD is the latest British pressing. It includes two bonus tracks, originally released as the band's only single (released on the same year of the album). The first music is reminiscent of early Pink Floyd psychedelia ? lighthearted, unpretentious, and breezy. The second track leans more towards The Moody Blues and Procol Harum vein; even the vocal style takes on a somewhat syrupy quality.General view of the CD: their technique isn't outstanding, and they lack a bit of variety on the instrumentation (however, they couldn't go so far on this matter, with only two members twogether). Their compositional habilities are exceptional, the arrangements are high-skilled, as well as most of the timbres.Rating: 4.1 of 5 stars.
items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的专辑将多种键盘乐器与鼓机的层次编织成充满张力的整体。开篇即以键盘乐句铺陈，后半段加入人声，融合了卡巴莱与布鲁斯摇滚的质感。乐队在编曲上颇具巧思：贝斯通过键盘与底鼓得以更清晰地呈现，鼓的过渡时刻揭示新的微妙层次。第六首以不同编排重现布鲁斯，键盘在混音中被巧妙突出；第七首以管风琴开场，营造出近乎灵性的氛围，是全碟最具灵感之作。第九首是对拉威尔《波莱罗》的Krautrock式浓缩改编，保留了原作的强度。终曲回归纯粹的Krautrock，电子和声与行进式鼓点自由交织。整体虽非创意与多样性的巅峰，但在键盘主导的实验性器乐框架内展现出扎实的作曲与编排功力。

items.album: Fuzzy Logic: K-drone by Šimanský Vaľko Podracký
items.tags: experimental electronic jazz world psych prog

items.body: Three explorers from the Czech-Slovak experimental music scene burrow deep into the woodland in search of some heady drones and – just maybe – a new experience of time itself Šimanský Vaľko Podracký pick up where Spacemen 3 left off. The Czech-Slovak trio of experimental musicians apparently share Pete Kember and Jason Pierce’s guiding principle of “taking drugs to make music to take drugs to”. The group’s psychedelia was inherited from the freewheeling 1960s, a decade when Western music – from rock to minimalism – was infused with the meditative transcendence of sustained tones. But the most important question is left unanswered: what drugs to take to make drone music to take drugs to? The album’s title may offer some cues. Born... items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由捷克-斯洛伐克实验音乐场景中的三位探索者完成，他们深入林野寻找浓烈的持续音，旨在提供一种全新的时间体验。乐队延续了Spacemen 3所奠定的传统，其迷幻美学源自1960年代自由奔放的风潮，彼时西方音乐——从摇滚到极简主义——都浸润在持续音所营造的冥想超越感之中。专辑标题暗示了某种药物文化的线索，将听觉沉浸与意识扩展紧密相连。整体作品以持续音为核心结构，强调声音的延展与空间的纵深感，在重复与微变之间探索聆听者的时间感知。这是一张为深度聆听而作的专辑，适合在安静环境中以开放心态进入其绵延的声响场域。

items.body: I’m lost in this sea of lies And every voice is pulling me The deeper that I sink below The harder it becomes to breathe A society driven by private desires gradually leads people to confuse exploitation with intelligence. Deception becomes a normal part of life, loyalty is conditional, and every interaction is seen as a strategic move for personal gain. For those still seeking genuine sincerity, this creates a strange sense of suffocation, as if each compromise raises the water level a little higher. “Drowning,” the newest single by Leipzig’s Kalte Steine, explores the psychological cost of moving through a culture increasingly shaped by self-interest, duplicity, and the pursuit of personal advantage at any cost. Continuing the English-language direction introduced on “Crying Out,” the track translates that social exhaustion into the sensation of sinking through an immeasurable body of water. The song opens with waves sighing against the shore before a bass line and drum machine enter, beating with the strained regularity of a heart short on oxygen. A quivering keyboard accent appears beside a simple melodic post-punk guitar figure, leaving broad spaces inside the arrangement. The economy of the playing and the grave tonal balance recall Pink Turns Blue at their starkest. The vocals drift in through delay and reverb, soft and mournful, with a natural English cadence settling easily across the meter. Their restraint suits the song’s depleted state, allowing “I’m drowning” to fall with the blunt force of an admission repeated too many times. The delivery stays low and controlled, placing fatigue at its expressive center. The lyrics recast dishonesty as an ocean without a visible boundary. Every voice pulls the singer deeper, the vanished shore removes any point of return, and the rising tide turns gradual ethical decay into a daily physical threat. “Lost in this sea of lies” describes both the surrounding culture and the point at which prolonged exposure to it has entered the body. Around the one-minute mark, the arrangement opens for the arrival of buzzing retro synthesizers, while the guitar flutters overhead like gulls crossing the waves. “The harder it becomes to breathe” is repeated, with the second delivery reduced to a whisper. Later, the same whispered echo follows “I’ve been drowning here for years,” changing a direct declaration into something barely confessed. In that sense, “Drowning” examines the exhaustion of preserving one’s humanity in a system that rewards manipulation. The plea to be taken beyond fear and washed clean of tears carries a desire for moral as well as physical escape. Years of submersion have left the song’s protagonist too tired to fight the tide, yet the act of identifying the water as a “sea of lies” preserves a final measure of clarity. “Drowning” is Kalte Steine’s most accomplished release so far. The songwriting holds its central metaphor from the first line to the last, the production grants each instrument greater definition, and the vocal performance gains authority through control. Those advances make its desolation more immediate, bringing sharper emotional and musical focus to the project’s familiar grey terrain. Listen to “Drowning” below: Kalte Steine’s previous singles—“Shattered,” “Dysthymia,” “Wüste aus Beton,” “Kinder der Nacht,” and “Crying Out”—established a monochrome world of private fracture, civic numbness, and nocturnal escape. As explored in our earlier feature on the project, those songs allowed inner conflict and a cold, dystopian exterior to blur into one another. “Drowning” is out now on all major streaming platforms. Follow Kalte Steine: Instagram Spotify SoundCloud TikTok The post “I’m Lost in This Sea of Lies” — Leipzig Darkwave Project Kalte Steine is Caught in a Deluge of Duplicity in “Drowning” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Kalte Steine的单曲《Drowning》以溺水隐喻在充满谎言与自利文化中的窒息感，延续了前作《Crying Out》的英文路线。歌曲以海浪声开场，贝斯与鼓机以缺氧般的心跳节奏进入，键盘与后朋克吉他留出大量空间，人声在延迟与混响中低沉游移，疲惫感成为表达核心。歌词将不诚实描绘为无边海洋，每一次妥协都让水位上升，反复出现的“我在溺水”逐渐从陈述变为耳语般的忏悔。中段加入复古合成器音色，吉他如海鸟般飘浮，整体编曲克制而富有画面感，被认为乐队迄今最成熟的作品。

items.body: “Vaga” came out of a London heatwave: a baião rhythm from Northeast Brazil, a maracatu-inspired groove, and a lift that recalls Sérgio Mendes. Lead vocalist Claudia Marques sings over a core of drums and keys, framing love as a boundless, constant current meant for everyone, with a roots-style female chorus behind her and flute lines over the top. Flautist Rachel Hayter weaves melodic lines alongside a backing chorus featuring Inês Loubet and Ana De Llor. Guitarist Jackson Caines, bassist Giovanni Cresseri, and drummer Jonny Venvell guide the arrangement into an energetic breakdown before tipping into a final key change. It is the first single from Novos Londrinos, a five-piece based in North London whose name nods to Novos Baianos, the Brazilian group from the 1970s, and reads as “new Londoners”. The players met in 2021 in a samba bateria, Rhythms of the City, then kept going through house jams, pulled together by 60s and 70s Brazilian music: the songwriting of Marcos Valle, the voice of Elis Regina. Their self-titled debut EP, recorded at Giant Wafer and Abbey Road Studios, reaches past bossa nova and samba into baião, spiritual jazz and Cape Verdean rhythms. Across it, Claudia Marques writes between lightness and introspection, turning over new arrivals, the passing of time, and the beautiful and unfamiliar. They played Glastonbury in 2025 and shared a Porto stage with Ivan Lins‘s bassist. On 22 November, they take a London Jazz Festival slot at Milton Court. Stream “Vaga” and get your copy of their debut EP HERE The post Daily Discovery: Novos Londrinos – Vaga appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Words by Justin TurfordIt’s bloody hard work trying to exist as a musician these days. Not ‘slave working in a coltan mine’ hard but tricky enough to navigate a world that has decided that music (and creativity in general) is something no longer worth paying the creator for. One musician who has regularly and bravely shared his own struggles about life in the independent music business is South Londoner Adam Scrimshire who if you don’t yet know then you should. A co-founder of the label Wah Wah 45s and now the one-man label head of Albert’s Favourites, an excellent record label dedicated to his own releases and a swathe of artists united by an emotional sensitivity and love for the deeper end of the groove pool, he is an underappreciated talent and a fine example of quiet determination.Over the years he has covered a lot of musical bases. From the soulful guest vocalist excursions of 2019’s ‘Listeners’ to the frustrated fury and free jazz-channeling collaborations with Idris Rahman, Nat Birchall and Tamar Osborne on 2021’s ‘Paroxysm’, Adam has proved adept at creating real music with real heart and emotion. The sheer number of top class collaborators who have been attracted to his orbit reveals an artist and producer of great taste and empathy. A successful collaboration takes more than an invitation to succeed.Here, on his ninth album, Adam has pushed through and overcome his doubts once again to deliver, in my opinion, his masterpiece. Five years in the making,  'Bring Our Light To Every Corner' contains six beautiful compositions of reflective soul, spiritual jazz and pastoral folk, awash with love and a much needed sense of unhurried time. Despite clearly drawing on the musical language of the late 60s and 70s psyche-soul-jazz-folk crossover period, the album never feels like he is trying to recreate an aesthetic. Without sounding like them directly, the record shares the DNA of 70s artists such as Stepney-era Terry Callier, Nick Drake and Pentangle, songwriters who understood the inherent romance of nature and how small stories reveal larger truths. We could also throw into the mix the widescreen sonic cinema of Arthur Verocai, Isaac Hayes or the Siberian musical traveller Misha Sultan: musician-arrangers with a knack for knowing when to keep it simple and when to go fully baroque.  “I wanted to create somewhere people could stay for a while.. A space that carries you gently through the record.”Space is certainly the place on the David Axelrod-channelling album starter, ‘My Land Is Your Land, Your Sky Is My Sky’. Chris Boot’s measured drums sit tight and loud over a slow-moving groove of tremolo guitar, sustained keys, Mark Zentai’s electric sitar and a brooding bass and piano riff that DJ Shadow could only dream about. Soprano saxophonist Jake Telford brings a searching, ecstatic energy as the song lifts from the Earth.The legendary Los Angeles jazz singer Dwight Trible brings his wordless Leon Thomas-like voicing to the cosmic hallucination of ‘Asleep, A Dream’. Also joined by harpist Amanda Whiting and Idris Rahman on flute and saxophone, Adam has created a timeless slice of funky, spiritual soul jazz with afrobeat-esque drums, huge strings and cheeky clavinet and Moog twiddling to add to the fun. A piece of music that makes me want to smile deeply.The title track ‘Bring Our Light To Every Corner’ is a handclapping communal singalong with a choir comprised of Rob Hynd, Daudi Matsiko, Jay Brown and Faye Houston joining Adam in a warming embrace of “La La La’s” over a delicate acoustic guitar, congas, hand percussion and vintage synths (all played by Adam). Churchy but earthy, it sits somewhere between Alice Coltrane’s funky mantras on her 1977 LP ‘Transcendence’ and the more pared back tracks of Leeds’ Ancient Infinity Orchestra. Needless to say, I love this vibe.The ever-brilliant keys maestro Jessica Lauren locks down her piano chops on the jazz-gospel-Northern soul bumper ‘With Our Eternal Hope And Joy’. Joined again by a (slightly different) choir and Idris Rahman on flute and sax, the song pulsates with the hope and joyfulness of its title. The main melodic hook is a beauty and when Joshu Idehen steps in to add some words of positive power before the late surge of full band energy, I can only wish that I had been in that room.‘Your Heart Is My Heart, My Hand Is Your Hand’ is an incredibly beautiful piece of meditative music. Adam plays his Rhodes with a subdued grace as Indian classical vocalist Mahesh Kale delicately invokes Shanti whilst shivers of strings and Jake Telford’s soprano saxophone electrifies the air. The album is only six songs strong but its concluding composition more than makes up for it. ‘Awake, A Dream’ is a spectacular epic made up of three distinct movements and comes in just shy of fifteen minutes long. The first third is a symphonic dream of pastoral bliss with acoustic guitar, piano and sweeping strings, long-time collaborator Faye Houston’s soulful harmonic voicing adding a woozy romance to this section. Silence. Chris Boot’s tight breakbeat and Adam’s picked bass enter the stage as Rhodes, acoustic guitar and stacked layers of Faye’s celestial voice unfurl and fill the atmosphere. The groove inhales and exhales for just the right amount of time before falling into a slumbering piano line, inviting Faye to step to the front. “Everything that we, everything that we dream” she sings with increasing urgency, high sustained strings and her own rich backing vocals shimmering like vibrations on water. Adam thinks this may be his favourite piece of music he’s made to date and I’m not surprised. It’s quite magnificent.There is a lot of great music being released this year but I suspect when I’ve forgotten some of those records (as you do), ‘Bring Our Light To Every Corner’ will be remembered as one of the best albums of 2026. 10/10.BUY HERE! https://scrimshire.bandcamp.com/album/bring-our-light-to-every-corner
items._cn_summary: Adam Scrimshire的第九张专辑历经五年打磨，收录六首融合灵魂乐、精神爵士与田园民谣的作品。乐评指出，专辑虽明显借鉴上世纪六七十年代迷幻灵魂爵士与民谣交叉时期的音乐语言，却并非刻意复刻某种美学，而是与Terry Callier、Nick Drake等创作脉络共享内在基因。开篇曲以沉稳鼓组、颤音吉他、电西塔琴与低音钢琴riff构建出缓慢流动的空间感，萨克斯风带来上升的即兴能量，洛杉矶爵士歌手Dwight Trible则以无词人声增添宇宙氛围。整体呈现一种不急于推进的时间感，强调情感敏感性与律动深处的人文关怀，体现创作者在独立音乐生态中坚持个人表达的安静决心。

items.body:
Daria Lourd (Bored Lord) + her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls = DARLYNN on their debut shot of Jersey club meets ‘90s R&B, woozy garage house and vintage psych-funk flavours.

"Darlynn is an Oakland-based duo composed of Daria Lourd (aka Bored Lord) and her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls. Dyke Den is a lesbian love story about two creative individuals finding each other and themselves through effusive and contemplative sonic avenues. Created in their home over the course of two years, this album speaks to the journey of Daria and Jaelynn’s romantic relationship as well as their evolving combined creative impulses.

On Dyke Den, Darlynn display their influences – from Janet Jackson and Sly & the Family Stone, to Frankie Knuckles and Larry Levan – in a sophisticated, fully realized, and overtly queered fashion. Joyous dancefloor moments are abundant. Tracks like “Make Yr Move” and “Like A Summer” celebrate deep house vibes ala Alleviated Records, while sultry R&B moves are flexed on “Girl 2 Girl” and “Alright With Me.” But longing and yearning exist within this joyous arc, and the question arises: “How can I get you to love me?” More than an idealistic narrative of girl meets they/them, Dyke Den paints a portrait of love in all its multifaceted moments: the bids for commitment, the stagnation of years going by, the wormholes of desire. Yet the album maintains its thesis of hope. The sweet, layered harmonies of closing song “Love Letter” display the power of life partnership: “My whole life is a love letter to you.” Dyke Den features artwork by Hailee Va in a sleeve designed by Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh. Darlynn’s final declaration, “We are all creatures of desire, completely built for love.”s"

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Oakland双人组Darlynn的处女作，由Bored Lord的Daria Lourd与歌手Jaelynn Walls合作完成，以Jersey club、90年代R&B、迷幻车库house和复古放克为基底，讲述两人从相遇到相恋的历程。作品在两年内于家中制作，融合了Janet Jackson、Sly & the Family Stone、Frankie Knuckles等影响，以鲜明的酷儿视角呈现舞池时刻与深情段落。歌曲如《Make Yr Move》《Like A Summer》偏向深邃house，而《Girl 2 Girl》《Alright With Me》展现柔滑R&B；同时也不回避渴望与停滞等复杂情感，最终以《Love Letter》的和声收束，强调伴侣关系中的承诺与希望。整体上，专辑在愉悦的舞池能量与内省的情感表达之间取得平衡，展示了两人作为生活与创作伴侣的默契。

items.body:
Michael J. Blood lends two rugged, tumping takes to Intertoto’s rudely groggy beatdown house

‘If I Take You Home’ is the first cut from London’s Intertoto since his well received album ‘Thermal Shadow’ (2023) and continues down a midnight path of mid-tempo, strutting beatdown roughly guided by likes of NWAQ and Kassel Mosse.

MJB steps it up a gear or two in a ‘Walk of Shame Mix’ built from woodcut kicks and gritty sampler revs plus additional vox like Martin Rev just walked in the room and did a Travolta “huh?”, plus a banging ‘Morning After Mix’ cloaked in muffled party noise and prompting jelly legs back to the ‘floor.
items._cn_summary: 这张混音EP将Intertoto的原作拆解为两个截然不同的版本。Walk of Shame Mix以木击鼓和粗粝的采样器声效为骨架，加入类似Martin Rev式的人声插段，制造出突兀而有力的节奏冲击；Morning After Mix则用闷噪的派对环境声包裹律动，营造出舞池散场后的余韵与肢体疲惫感。两个版本延续了午夜质感的行进节奏，在NWAQ和Kassel Mosse的影响路径上推进，体现了MJB对舞曲结构的实验性重塑，以及声音材质上的粗粝美学，适合关注地下舞曲与实验电子交叉领域的听众。

items.body:
Josephine Foster and the Victor Herrero Band release "Anda Jaleo" via Fire Records.

"A live recording of “Las Canciones”; a visceral celebration of the persistence of popular anonymous song based on the work of legendary socialist poet Federico García Lorca, a Granada born literary pioneer. Featuring songs from his 1931 collection of mysteriously beautiful flamenco tunes. A poetically rich collection created by Foster and Herrero for their acoustic band, formed while living in the Grenadine Sierra. “Foster’s vocals, met by husband Herrero’s frantic and raw gypsy-band orchestration, demonstrates the sense of urgency in the music’s message well and carries ‘Anda Jaleo’ to an elevated state.” The Line Of Best Fit... “The alt-folk fixture returns to more traditional material.” Pitchfork." "
items._cn_summary: 这张现场录音专辑以西班牙诗人洛尔迦1931年收集的弗拉门戈歌曲为素材，由Josephine Foster与Victor Herrero的声学乐队在格拉纳达山区创作并演绎。Foster的人声与Herrero狂放原始的吉普赛乐队编曲相互交织，赋予这些匿名流传的古老歌曲以强烈的现场紧迫感。专辑并非简单的民歌复刻，而是通过诗意的文本选择和即兴化的器乐编排，让传统曲调在当代语境中重新获得生命力。对于关注世界音乐与民间音乐现场表现力的听众，这张作品提供了对西班牙南部音乐遗产的一种鲜活、粗粝的聆听体验。

items.body:
Josephine Foster and the Victor Herrero Band release "Perlas" via Fire Records.

"Their follow up to the acclaimed ‘Anda Jaleo’. A document of Josephine Foster's magical partnership with Victor Herrero breathing new life into timeless traditional melodies, drawing from the Spanish-folk traditions of Castile, the Basque, Santander and the Costa Brava. ‘Perlas’ is debonair, contemporary and redolent of that old seductive charge.” The Wire. Elemental themes of love bind the collection together, with a melancholy joy that casts a shadow of desire and loss. “The alt- folk fixture returns to more traditional material.” Pitchfork."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Josephine Foster与Victor Herrero乐队继《Anda Jaleo》后的合作，以当代视角重新演绎卡斯蒂利亚、巴斯克、桑坦德和布拉瓦海岸的西班牙传统民谣。作品在保留古老旋律韵味的同时注入新的生命力，编曲简洁而富有魅力。主题围绕爱展开，在忧郁与喜悦之间交织出欲望与失落的阴影。Foster的另类民谣根基在此回归更传统的素材，整体呈现出现代与传统之间的张力。作为独立厂牌发行，专辑延续了两人在西班牙民间音乐领域的探索。

items.body:
Another bite-sized teaser of Chang's upcoming 'been thinking bout confession', 'Bad zen' packages the soaring title track with a handful of the album's other singles.

If you need more convincing before you dig into the full length, this should do the job. 'Bad zen' is actually one of the album's more restrained tracks, led by Chang's most melancholy vocal turn that she accompanies with wobbly synth strings and jazzy guitars. Compared with 'Auratones of Desire', that's also bundled on the EP, it's practically horizontal - thank goodness there's 'No avatar', the album's most chewable track, included too.
items._genre: art pop / experimental / jazz fusion / synth pop
items._cn_summary: 这张EP以短小体量预览了即将发行的专辑，收录标题曲及另外两首单曲。标题曲是专辑中较为内敛的一首，以忧郁的人声为主导，搭配摇摆的合成器弦乐与爵士吉他，整体氛围沉静。相比之下，同收录的《Auratones of Desire》更具动态与张力，形成鲜明反差；而《No avatar》则被描述为专辑中最易入耳的作品，提供了更直接的聆听入口。整体上，EP在忧郁抒情与更具嚼劲的曲目之间取得平衡，展现了艺术家在合成器音色、爵士和声与独立流行框架间的游走，适合对实验性流行与爵士融合感兴趣的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以难民与安置工作者的真实话语为核心素材，将作曲与纪录片实践紧密结合。艺术家此前长期关注亚美尼亚种族灭绝、叙利亚难民危机与黎巴嫩内战等议题，作品带有鲜明的社会政治视角。声音设计上融合了人声采样、环境声响与器乐写作，在当代古典框架内引入纪实性叙事，形成介于音乐文献与声音剧场之间的独特形态。该作曾入围普利策奖决赛，体现了其艺术价值与议题深度。对于关注现代作曲、实验声响及跨媒介叙事的听众而言，这是一部具有文化重量和形式探索意义的作品。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The world's first and pre-eminent Jazz-Rock band releases their first album, thanks to Columbia Records, on February 28, 1968. Led by multi-instrumentalist musical genius Al Kooper and former Blues Project mate Steve Katz. The band was focused and committed to sporting a James Brown-like horn section as well as orchestral accompaniments. 1. "Overture" (1:33) talk about a Frank Zappa influence! This is classical symphonic music with a track of uncontrolled laughter (one might say, lunacy). It's taking The Beatles' George Martin effect and Frank Zappa eclectic skills and absurdism to new levels! (4.625/5)2. "I Love You More Than You'll Ever Know" (5:58) blues-based organ, bass & drums with electric rock guitar and very skilled lead vocals. What a great James Brown-like horn arrangement, great female background vocal "ooo's," great guitar sounds (both lead and rhythm) as well as a very zoned-in lead vocal of some powerful lyrics from Al Kooper. The finale is incredible! I wish it weren't faded out. Wow! This kind of perfection I was not expecting (from a debut album launched in 1968). (10/10)3. "Morning Glory" (4:15) a solid, polished, professional song that does little to (9/10)4. "My Days Are Numbered" (3:18) a song whose Soul gravity predicts the band's monster hits of the near future as well as sounding exactly like Paul Weller's transitional music from The Jam to The Style Council, it's is blessed with an amazingly intricate overal construct of multiple motifs all arranged and performed with such feeling, plus possessing an amazingly-catchy chorus. (9.75/10)5. "Without Her" (2:41) the jazzy/lounge side of the band with a poppy Brit-Pop swing to it and more distinctly-defined individual instrumental sounds and performances (piano, bass, jazz drums, trumpet, sax, close intimate vocal performance) as well as Jobim-like Spanish guitar play serving as the rhythm guitar. Awesome both musically and as an brainworm. (10/10)6. "Just One Smile" (4:37) another wonderfully-arranged and -rendered musical landscape with more of Jim Fielder's awesome electric bass play, Al's vulnerable and emotional vocal and incredible horn section . Weirdly, the chorus is the song's weakest element as it doesn't quite deliver the promise that the verses seem to build toward. I love the little Baroque interplay of the lute and keyboard in the instrumental passage in the first half of the fourth minute! (9.375/10) 7. "I Can't Quit Her" (3:39) opening with some Burt Bacharach like piano play of a few chords before the bass and drums enter, followed soon thereafter by Al's reverb-treated vocal and the accents of the Beatles-like horn section. Strings and female choir back the first chorus section before routing the band back into a repeat of the verse section. Then around 2:30 there is a powerful transition to a heavier, more emotional instrumental section which plays out to the final fade-out of the music with no other return of the vocal/lyrics. Awesome! What creative song construction! (9.25/10) 8. "Meagan's Gypsy Eyes" (3:24) starting out with gently-picked acoustic guitar the song then amps up with the arrival of horns and a weird keyboard. There are ample effects applied to the anachronistic keys and doubled-up vocal track, this song travels with a fairly thin and simple psychedelic sound palette until the chorus when the horns and strings get involved. This sounds a lot like something from DONOVAN, The 13th Floor Elevators, or even one of the British Baroque Pop making their way across The Pond. Steve Katz' lead vocal is great for the delivery of the song's folkie-psychedelic lyrics but he's nowhere near as strong or powerful as Al Kooper; he's more of a gnome-like delivery person. Still, this is a cool, interesting, and, ultimately, memorable song. (9/10)9. "Something' Going On" (8:00) pure JAMES BROWN bluesy R&B with each and every instrument being asked to play at their loudest and most concise/compact forms while Al sings a purely blues-oriented . Steve Katz' electric guitar solo in the third minute is surprisingly loud while also benefitting from enough distortion to make it sound like something between Eric Clapton and Jimi Hendrix. Even Steve's ensuing rhythm guitar play behind Al's piano solo in the fourth minute is loud: way louder than Al's piano. The horns, too, are really loud as Al returns to the vocal, singing as if he's trying to incite some loud audience participation/response. Tenor sax starts to solo beneath Al's call & response-like vocals. At the end of the seventh minute the music thins and returns to the form of the opening section for the band and Al to pull it to a close--but then they really ramp things up again for the finish! Great drumming from Bobby Colomby! (13.25/15) 10. "House In The Country" (3:04) a peppy little song that with multiple vocal tracks that sounds like something from a sophisticated British pop band (not The Stones or Who, more Beatles) and then they inject some of the the Zappa-like absurdist humor with ancillary voice-acted tracks. Interesting. (8.875/10) 11. "The Modern Adventures Of Plato, Diogenes And Freud" (4:12) delicate voice with chamber strings support again remind one of British Baroque Pop bands as Al sings over the top with a sincerity and literacy that sounds/feels like contemporary social commentary poetry being sung (but, again, previews an artist like Paul Weller). (9/10)12. "So Much Love / Underture" (4:43) a bit of a PROCOL HARUM sound and feel to this as Jim and Bobby lay down a funky David Axelrod-like rhythm track with Al's organ and Steve's twangy rhythm guitar strokes. Horns and background choir vocals join in from time to time, usually in bridges and sometimes in the verse passages and then over the choruses. For the final 90 seconds there is a simple pulsing organ note punctuated by brass chord blasts before the strings and weird organ oscillation sounds join in. Could've come from a West End musical. (8.75/10) Total time 49:24There are many times when the clever, sophisticated songs on this album remind me of the genius of artists like The Moody Blues, Pete Townsend, Paul McCartney, Brian Auger, and James Brown.A/five stars; a ground-breaking masterpiece of R&B/Rock Fusion (what we've all come to refer to as "Brass Rock"), one of the finest debut albums to ever explode onto the 1960s music scene.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Blood Sweat and Tears于1968年发行的首张作品，由Al Kooper和Steve Katz主导，将爵士摇滚、灵魂乐、管乐编曲与古典管弦乐元素融为一体。乐评指出其受到Frank Zappa的荒诞感与Beatles制作手法的双重影响，开篇序曲即带有实验性的古典交响段落。歌曲结构普遍复杂，如《My Days Are Numbered》融合多个动机与情绪段落，《I Can't Quit Her》从Bacharach式钢琴过渡到重型的器乐高潮。铜管组被赋予类似James Brown式节奏冲击力，同时穿插巴洛克式鲁特琴与键盘对话、Jobim风格西班牙吉他等细节。专辑在1968年即以高度成熟的编曲和跨类型整合能力，成为爵士摇滚融合领域的重要早期样本，展现了摇滚乐队引入爵士和古典语汇的多种可能性。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Vanden Plas playing progressive metal before its time. This 13th album, a cathedral of sound, picks up where the acoustic "AcCult" left off 30 years later."Far Off Grace," from the album of the same name, shines on the acoustic guitar, which understood that more than just noise was needed. Stephan excels, Alessandro captivates, Andy enchants with his uniquely melancholic voice; the Andalusian solo before the furious finale, restrained, neoclassical, progressive, hypnotic layering these musical textures. "Holes in the Sky" from "Seraphic Clockwork" follows the same pattern, a slow, melodic build-up stripped of electric guitar; a relaxing track with a 6-string acoustic solo. Andy's warm vocals make this a radical departure from the original heavy metal vibe. "The Ghost Experiment" has a Maiden United feel, with the drums letting the bass drums lay down the rhythm and power. An Andalusian, Celtic, and refined folk solo, captivating, oscillates between drama and melancholic joy. "Boat on the River," a Styx cover, accentuates the Celtic feel, the introspective guitar, the accordion a poignant memory, sailing between the Balkans, Greece, and a New Orleans port."Healing Tree" from "Beyond Daylight" features crystalline piano and a cinematic atmosphere with the flute. A vocal duet ballad by Andy and Katri from Numento, the female voice. The piano, the two-tone break, the solemn, archaic prog on Marillion, the Irish flute. Memory, relaxation, wisdom, emphasis. "Postcard to God" from "Christ 0" is a crystalline stereo-melodic vibration with shifting tempos. Andy leads this mellowed metal ship, while Stephan weaves in a folk tune before Alessandro's pre-Genesisian, saccharine solo. "Nothing Else Matters" features a stripped-down piano guiding Andy down a new dramatic path, the dark strings adding to its delicate sensitivity. A stunning Metallica cover, giving you goosebumps. "You Fly" from "The God Thing," piano and guitar, Maiden United again?go listen to them. The complex track, richer with its velvety keyboards and the surprising addition of John's sax from Supertramp. The sensual, contemplative melody, the captivating guitar-saxophone break, the almost heavy bass rhythm?a musical paradigm. The latent, progressive build-up, the sustained riff, the piano and saxophone solo?reminiscent of '80s Phil Collins and Dire Straits. A fresh, jazzy, marshmallowy feel that culminates in a wild, heavy finale. (3.75)

items._cn_summary: 德国前卫金属乐队 Vanden Plas 将过往作品以木琴化方式重新演绎，并收录两首翻唱。原曲的失真电吉他被原声吉他、钢琴、长笛、手风琴与萨克斯取代，人声保留忧郁特质，节奏与和声转向凯尔特、安达卢西亚、巴尔干及新奥尔良等民间音乐色彩，同时维持前卫金属的结构复杂度。Styx 与 Metallica 的翻唱被重塑为室内乐式的叙事，多首曲目在慢速铺陈中引入爵士萨克斯独奏与即兴段落，形成从民谣到前卫摇滚的宽阔跨度。乐评逐曲解析了改编手法，强调其以 acoustic 为媒介将重型音乐转化为细腻织体的能力，并指出部分段落带有 Marillion、Maiden United 等乐队的影子。整体上这是一次对自身作品的重构，在保留前卫骨架的同时注入了更多世界音乐与爵士元素。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — If one goes back in time to the very early days of Martin Springett the musician, he was in a band called Gateway Driver in 1973 and played in Germany with bassist Rob Burns. Rob later worked with the likes of David Gilmour, Pete Townshend, and Eric Burdon, was professor at Otago University as well as being an author of different books on music. When Martin released the wonderful 'The Gardening Club' album in 1983, the keyboard player John Sheard, who has since appeared on hundreds of recordings with artists such as, Rita Mcneil, Olivia Newton-John, Ian and Sylvia, Dan Hill, Rita Coolidge, Mary Margaert O'Hara, Celine Dion, and many more. This song came about after Martin survived a major heart operation, and now he is again fighting various issues he decided to finally complete the song, as he always liked it but never felt there was room for it on 'The Riddle'. In many ways he has used musicians who document the journey he has been through, as alongside Rob and John we also have Kevin Laliberte who has worked closely with Martin for the last five years. The quartet may never have been in the same room together (Rob still lives in NZ and the rest of the guys are in Canada), but it never feels that way, as here they sound as if the band are playing and smiling at each other as they work through a song which never feels as if it is more than eight minutes long. It is undoubtedly one of Martin's finest pieces to date, wonderfully layered with the warmth of Camel combining with some of the detachment of Pink Floyd, all brought together with stacks of Roy Harper to make something which is truly special. I found the best way to truly appreciate this song is to put it on repeat and just let it play for a few hours as each time there is something else which comes to light, making this majestic and wonderful. Is it the multi-tracked and slightly distorted slide guitars here, or the layered keyboards there, the feeling that Martin's acoustic guitar and vocals are always at the heart of everything, with bass which is warm and reflective, driving when needed to?I have no idea, but yet again I can only wonder what would have happened if 'The Gardening Club' had received the credit it so richly deserved more than 40 years ago. Would Martin now be a household name in the music industry? Given the quality (and remarkable quantity) of his output since 2018 I can only imagine. I know I feel warmed by his friendship and feel real joy and empathy when listening to songs such as this. This is currently only available as a digital single on Bandcamp, and for just $2 what have you got to lose? If you know his music then you will delight in this, and if you have yet to come across Martin then this is the perfect introduction.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这首单曲源自Martin Springett在1983年《The Gardening Club》时期未完成的创作，在经历重大心脏手术后重新拾起并最终完成。参与录音的乐手包括早年乐队伙伴贝斯手Rob Burns、键盘手John Sheard以及长期合作者Kevin Laliberte，尽管成员分处新西兰与加拿大，录音却呈现出同处一室的默契。作品以原声吉他与 vocals 为核心，叠加多轨滑音吉他、层次丰富的键盘以及温暖而富有驱动力的贝斯，整体气质兼具Camel的温润与Pink Floyd的疏离感，并带有Roy Harper式的民谣叙事色彩。乐评认为这是Martin最出色的作品之一，长度超过八分钟却不觉冗长，反复聆听能不断发现新的细节。该曲目前以数字单曲形式在Bandcamp发行。

items.body: ÆRIA released “Ivy” on August 4, 2026, the second of six tracks on the self-released EP “Ivy: The First Mini-Album”. The project mixes operatic vocals with synthpop basslines and coldwave textures, and describes itself on its own YouTube channel as “an operatic darkwave girl group from a fantasy music universe”. No label is credited: the copyright and phonogram lines on the release both read ÆRIA. What is on ÆRIA’s ‘Ivy: The First Mini-Album’ The EP runs 19 minutes and 26 seconds across six tracks: “Stargirls (Intro)” (1:30), “Ivy” (3:25), “Bright Side Of The Moon” (4:04), “In Her Hands” (4:46), “Ivy (Reprise)” (3:12) and “Stargirls (Outro)” (2:27). The two “Stargirls” pieces bracket the record and “Ivy” returns in a reprise, so the running order is built as a single arc rather than a set of separate songs. The release is on Spotify; no physical edition and no Bandcamp page have been confirmed. The band’s own promotional material presents “Ivy” as a debut single. On the release itself it appears as an album track, and the EP carries a single date of August 4, 2026 for all six pieces. The accompanying “ÆRIA – IVY (Official Music Video)” runs 3:27 and was posted to the group’s YouTube channel, which also carries a short clip titled “How ÆRIA Began”. About ÆRIA ÆRIA is a new project with a short public record, so much of its history is not yet documented. What is confirmed comes from the group’s own channels and from the release itself. The project presents itself as a fantasy girl group whose music, artwork and narrative are built as one continuous story, and it states openly that it is AI-rendered, describing the technology as an artistic canvas rather than something to conceal. Correspondence sent to press on behalf of the project is signed by a member using the name Cerulean Blue. The group maintains a YouTube channel at @weareaeria, an Instagram account at @weareaeria and a TikTok account at @aeriaband. Its first release, “Ivy: The First Mini-Album”, arrived on August 4, 2026 without a label, distributor or producer credit attached to it. Side-Line previously covered a comparable case in The mysterious case of Ella Rey – An AI darkwave artist, where an AI-generated darkwave project built a substantial streaming audience without disclosing how the recordings were made; ÆRIA differs in stating the method up front. No live dates, further releases or member names have been announced.
items._cn_summary: ÆRIA是一支公开以AI技术生成并自称“歌剧暗潮女团”的新项目，其首张EP《Ivy: The First Mini-Album》于2026年8月4日自发行，共六首曲目，总长19分26秒。作品以两段“Stargirls”首尾呼应，并包含主打曲“Ivy”及其再现版，整体结构呈现单一叙事弧。音乐上融合歌剧式人声、合成流行贝斯线与冷潮质感，营造出兼具戏剧性与暗黑氛围的声音场景。项目明确将AI视为艺术媒介而非隐藏手段，并以幻想宇宙为整体世界观。目前该EP仅上线Spotify，无厂牌、实体或Bandcamp页面。文章为新闻式介绍，侧重发行信息与项目背景，未对音乐细节展开深度评论。
